questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt:
THE FIBRES OF THE INTERNAL OBLIQUE MUSCLE AND TRANSVERSE ABDOMINUS MUSCLE CONTRIBUTE TO
WHICH BOUNDARIES OF THE INGUINAL CANAL WALLS:
questions.explanation:
THE FIBRES OF THE INTERNAL OBLIQUE MUSCLE AND TRANSVERSE ABDOMINUS MUSCLE CONTRIBUTE TO THE ROOF
AND POSTERIOR WALL OF THE INGUINAL CANAL WALLS.
THE BOUNDARIES OF THE INGUINAL CANAL WALLS ARE AS FOLLOWS:
- ANTERIOR WALL: FORMED BY THE EXTERNAL OBLIQUE APONEUROSIS.
- ROOF: FORMED BY THE ARCHED FIBRES OF THE INTERNAL OBLIQUE AND TRANSVERSUS ABDOMINIS MUSCLES.
- FLOOR: FORMED BY THE GROOVED UPPER SURFACE OF THE ABDOMEN AND PELVIS INGUINAL LIGAMENT.
- POSTERIOR WALL: CONSISTS OF THE TRANSVERSALIS FASCIA AND CONJOINT TENDON (THE LOWEST FIBRES OF THE
TRANSVERSES ABDOMINIS MUSCLE FUSE WITH THE LOWEST FIBRES OF THE INTERNAL OBLIQUE TO FORM THE
CONJOINT TENDON).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS A FUNCTION OF THE MARKED LAYER?
questions.explanation:
THE IMAGE SHOWS A HISTOLOGICAL SECTION OF THE ADRENAL GLAND AND THE LAYER MARKED IS THE OUTERMOST
LAYER, IE, THE ZONA GLOMERULOSA, WHICH SECRETES THE MINERALOCORTICOID - ALDOSTERONE, RESPONSIBLE FOR
SODIUM AND WATER RETENTION.
BASED ON STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION, THE ADRENAL CORTEX HAS THREE ZONES, WHICH FROM OUTER TO INNER,
ARE:
- ZONA GLOMERULOSA: SECRETES MINERALOCORTICOIDS (ALDOSTERONE) - WHICH ACTS IN RESPONSE TO THE
ACTIVATION OF THE RENIN-ANGIOTENSIN-ALDOSTERONE-SYSTEM (RAAS) AND ACTS AT THE DISTAL CONVOLUTED
TUBULE AND THE COLLECTING DUCTS FAVOURING SODIUM AND WATER RETENTION AND POTASSIUM EXCRETION.
352
- ZONA FASICULATA: SECRETES GLUCOCORTICOIDS (CORTISOL AND CORTICOSTERONE) - WHICH HAS MULTIPLE
FUNCTIONS THAT INCLUDE METABOLIC EFFECTS WHICH INDUCE HYPERGLYCEMIA INDUCING GLUCONEOGENESIS
(OPTION A) AND MEDIATES ANTI-INFLAMMATORY AND IMMUNOSUPPRESIVE EFFECTS BY INTERACTING WITH THE
CELLS OF THE IMMUNE SYSTEM (OPTION D).
- ZONA RETICULARIS: SECRETES SEX STEROIDS (DEHYDROEPIANDROSTERONE, ANDROSTENEDIONE, ESTROGENS,
AND GLUCOCORTICOIDS) (OPTION C)

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT'S RIGHT HIP DROPS WHEN HE TAKES THE RIGHT FOOT OFF THE GROUND. WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING
WOULD NOT BE INVOLVED IN THE PATIENT?
questions.explanation:
A PATIENT WITH DROPPING OF THE RIGHT HIP ON LIFTING THE RIGHT FOOT OFF THE GROUND, HAS A POSITIVE
TRENDELENBURG’S SIGN. THE SCIATIC NERVE WOULD NOT BE INVOLVED.
A POSITIVE TRENDELENBURG'S SIGN IS SEEN IN THE PARALYSIS OF THE GLUTEUS MEDIUS AND GLUTEUS MINIMUS
MUSCLES, BOTH OF WHICH ARE SUPPLIED BY THE SUPERIOR GLUTEAL NERVE. IN THE SCENARIO MENTIONED,
SINCE THE PATIENT HAS DROPPING OF THE HIP ON THE RIGHT SIDE, THE STRUCTURES ON THE LEFT SIDE WOULD BE
AFFECTED.
353
MECHANISM OF ACTIONS OF GLUTEUS MEDIUS AND MINIMUS:
- WHEN THE LEG ON ONE SIDE IS LIFTED OFF THE GROUND, MAKING IT THE UNSUPPORTED SIDE, GLUTEUS
MEDIUS AND MINIMUS MUSCLES ON THE OPPOSITE SIDE, WHICH IS THE SUPPORTED SIDE, EXERT TRACTION ON
THE HIP BONE BY ACTING FROM THE FEMUR. THIS ACTION RESULTS IN SLIGHT RAISING OF THE PELVIS ON THE
UNSUPPORTED SIDE, WHICH HELPS MAINTAIN THE TRUNK IN THE UPRIGHT POSITION.
- WHEN THE GLUTEUS MEDIUS AND MINIMUS ARE PARALYZED, THE PELVIS ON THE UNSUPPORTED SIDE SINKS
WHEN THE PATIENT LIFTS THE FOOT OFF THE GROUND. THIS CAUSES THE PATIENTS TO HAVE A CHARACTERISTIC
LURCHING GAIT.

questions.answer: IT OCCURS DUE TO THE PERSISTANCE OF PRECHORDAL PLATE
questions.explanation:
354
THE IMAGE SHOWS A SACROCOCCYGEAL TERATOMA, WHICH OCCURS DUE TO THE PERSISTENCE OF PLURIPOTENT
CELLS OF THE PRIMITIVE STREAK IN THE SACROCOCCYGEAL REGION.
DURING THE THIRD WEEK OF EMBRYOLOGICAL DEVELOPMENT, THE PROCESS OF GASTRULATION OCCURS, WHICH
REFERS TO THE FORMATION OF THE THREE GERM LAYERS. THESE GERM LAYERS ARE FORMED FROM THE
PRIMORDIAL GERM CELLS OF THE EPIBLAST, WHICH ARE PLURIPOTENT. THE PROCESS BEGINS WITH THE
FORMATION OF THE PRIMITIVE STREAK ON THE EPIBLAST, WHICH DEVELOPS INTO THE PRIMITIVE NODE IN THE
CRANIAL REGION, AND A PRIMITIVE PIT. THE CELLS FROM THE EPIBLAST, MIGRATE TOWARDS THE PRIMITIVE
STREAK AND INVAGINATE INTO THE PRIMITIVE PIT AND ORGANIZES ITSELF INTO CELLS ARRANGED IN THREE LAYERS,
WHICH EVENTUALLY DEVELOP INTO ECTODERM, MESODERM, AND ENDODERM. THE PRECHORDAL PLATE SIMPLY
REFERS TO THE CELLS THAT HAVE INVAGINATED IN THE CRANIAL REGION.
SACROCOCCYGEAL TERATOMAS OCCUR DUE TO REMNANTS OF PLURIPOTENT CELLS FROM THE PRIMITIVE STREAK DUE
TO DEFECTIVE MIGRATION OF THE CELLS (OPTION B). AS THESE CELLS ARE FROM THE EPIBLAST, TERATOMAS
CONTAIN TISSUES FROM ALL GERM LAYERS WHICH MAY INCLUDE SKIN, HAIR, CARTILAGE AND BONE (OPTION C).
THESE TUMORS ARE BENIGN IN NATURE (OPTION D), BUT MAY RARELY BECOME MALIGNANT. IF THEY OCCUR IN
THE CRANIAL END OF THE PRIMITIVE STREAK, THEY FORM ORO-PHARYNGEAL TERATOMAS (AS SHOWN BELOW),
WHEREAS IF THEY OCCUR IN THE CAUDAL END OF THE PRIMITIVE STREAK IN THE COCCYGEAL REGION, THEY ARE
CALLED SACRO-COCCYGEAL TERATOMAS.
355

questions.prompt: IDENTIFY THE ARROW-MARKED STRUCTURE.
questions.explanation:
THE ARROW MARKS THE BIFURCATION OF THE PULMONARY TRUNK.
THE IMAGE SHOWS A CROSS SECTION OF A CADAVER AT THE T5 VERTEBRAL LEVEL. THIS CORRESPONDS ANTERIORLY
TO THE LEVEL OF THE STERNAL ANGLE, AND IS ALSO THE LEVEL OF DIVISION BETWEEN THE SUPERIOR AND INFERIOR
MEDIASTINUM.
AT THIS LEVEL, THE OTHER STRUCTURES VISIBLE ARE:
- THE ORIGIN AND TERMINATION OF THE ARCH OF AORTA. THE DESCENDING AORTA CAN BE IDENTIFIED TO THE LEFT
OF THE OESOPHAGUS. THE ARCH OF THE AORTA (OPTION D) WOULD BE VISIBLE AT THE T3-T4 CROSS SECTIONAL
LEVEL.
- THE SUPERIOR VENA CAVA (OPTION B), JUST LATERAL TO THE ORIGIN OF THE AORTA, WHICH CAN VISUALLY
DIFFERENTIATED FROM THE AORTA BASED ON THE WALL THICKNESS. AT THIS LEVEL, IT PENETRATES THE RIGHT
ATRIUM.
- THE BIFURCATION OF THE PULMONARY TRUNK.
- THE LEFT AND RIGHT MAIN BRONCHI. THE CARINA (OPTION A) IS NOT VISIBLE AS THE TRACHEA BIFURCATES
MORE PROXIMALLY AT THE T4 LEVEL.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: WHAT IS THE ROLE OF THE MARKED STRUCTURE IN THE GIVEN IMAGE?
questions.explanation:
THE MARKED STRUCTURE IS THE SUBTHALAMIC NUCLEUS, WHICH IS A PART OF THE BASAL GANGLIA AND IS
CONCERNED WITH MOTOR FUNCTION.
THE BASAL GANGLIA REFERS TO THE MASS OF GREY MATTER LOCATED WITHIN THE CEREBRAL WHITE MATTER AND IS
RESPONSIBLE FOR A NUMBER OF COORDINATED FUNCTIONS INCLUDING THE CONTROL OF EXTRA-PYRAMIDAL
PATHWAYS FOR MOTOR COORDINATION. THERE ARE TWO MAJOR PATHWAYS INVOLVED WHICH ARE, THE DIRECT
AND INDIRECT PATHWAYS.
THE DIRECT PATHWAY STIMULATES THE CORTEX TO PRODUCE MOVEMENT, WHEREAS THE INDIRECT PATHWAY
INHIBITS IT. THE STRIATAL ACTIVITY IN THE DIRECT PATHWAY IS MEDIATED BY D1 DOPAMINE RECEPTORS AND IN
THE INDIRECT PATHWAY BY D2 DOPAMINE RECEPTORS. THE SUBTHALAMIC NUCLEUS IS A PART OF THE INDIRECT
PATHWAY. A LESION AT SUBTHALAMIC NUCLEI LEADS TO LOSS OF INHIBITORY EFFECT OF THE INDIRECT PATHWAY
RESULTING IN DOPAMINERGIC OVERACTIVITY RESPONSIBLE FOR FEATURES OF HEMIBALLISMUS.
357
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: REWARD-PUNISHMENT IS ASSOCIATED WITH THE PREFRONTAL AREA AND THE DOPAMINERGIC
CONNECTIONS LINKED TO IT FROM THE VENTRAL TEGMENTAL AREA.
OPTION C: JUDGEMENT IS CONTROLLED BY THE FRONTAL LOBE.
OPTION D: MEMORY IS CONTROLLED BY THE HIPPOCAMPUS.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: THE MARKED STRUCTURE SENDS EFFERENTS TO WHICH NUCLEUS OF THE THALAMUS?
questions.explanation:
THE MARKED STRUCTURE IN THE GIVEN CORONAL SECTION OF THE BRAIN IS THE FORNIX. THE FORNIX CARRIES
ASSOCIATIONS FROM THE HIPPOCAMPUS TO THE ANTERIOR NUCLEUS OF THE THALAMUS VIA THE MAMILLARY
BODIES.
THE PAPEZ CIRCUIT IS A PART OF THE LIMBIC SYSTEM CONCERNED WITH THE CONTROL OF EMOTIONAL BEHAVIOUR
AND MEMORY.
IT CONSISTS OF THE FOLLOWING STRUCTURES, WHICH CAN BE REMEMBERED USING THE GIVEN MNEMONIC:
- HIPPOCAMPUS (HE)
- MAMILLARY BODY (MAN)
- ANTERIOR THALAMUS (ATE)
- CINGULATE GYRUS (CAT)

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt:
ON NEUROLOGIC EXAMINATION, A PATIENT IS NOT ABLE TO IDENTIFY AN OBJECT BUT IS ABLE TO RECOGNIZE
THE OBJECT FROM ITS TEXTURE, COLOUR AND PATTERN. WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS LIKELY TO HAVE BEEN
AFFECTED?
questions.explanation:
THE CLINICAL SCENARIO SUGGESTS THAT THE PATIENT HAS VISUAL AGNOSIA AND THE LIKELY SITE OF INVOLVEMENT
WOULD BE THE INFERIOR TEMPORAL LOBE.
- AGNOSIA REFERS TO THE INABILITY TO VISUALLY IDENTIFY OBJECTS AND IS ALSO CALLED OPTIC APHASIA.
ACCORDING TO DE JONG, VISUAL AGNOSIA IS FURTHER CLASSIFIED INTO:
- APPERCEPTIVE VISUAL AGNOSIA - THE VISUAL IMAGE APPEARS DISTORTED TO THE PATIENT AND HENCE THEY
ARE UNABLE TO RECOGNISE IT. THIS OCCURS DUE LESIONS IN THE PARIETO-OCCIPITAL REGION
- ASSOCIATIVE VISUAL AGNOSIA - INABILITY TO VISUALLY IDENTIFY OBJECTS IN THE ABSENCE OF VISUAL
IMPAIRMENT, WITH ABILITY TO IDENTIFY THE OBJECT USING OTHER SENSORY MODALITIES (AS SUGGESTED IN THE
SCENARIO). THIS OCCURS DUE TO LESIONS OF OCCIPITO-TEMPORAL JUNCTION, WHICH IS PRESENT IN THE INFERIOR
TEMPORAL LOBE. PROSOPAGNOSIA IS A TYPE OF ASSOCIATETIVE VISUAL AGNOSIA WHICH REFERS TO THE
INABILITY TO VISUALLY IDENTIFY FACES.
THE OCCIPITAL LOBE ACTS AS THE PRIMARY VISUAL AREA AND A LESION IN THIS REGION WOULD RESULT IN
CORTICAL BLINDNESS AND ACHROMATOPSIA, WHICH IS THE INABILITY TO VISUALISE COLOUR. IN THE GIVEN
SCENARIO, AS THE PATIENT IS ALSO ABLE TO IDENTIFY COLOUR, IT INDICATES THAT THE OCCIPITAL LOBE (OPTION A)
IS UNAFFECTED AND (HENCE INFERIOR TEMPORAL LOBE IS THE BETTER ANSWER).
STEREOGNOSIS IS THE ABILITY TO IDENTIFY AN OBJECT BY A PERCEPTION OF THE FORM AND NATURE OF AN OBJECT
WITHOUT LOOKING AT IT. IN THE GIVEN SCENARIO, THE PATIENT IS ABLE TO RECOGNIZE THE OBJECT FROM ITS
TEXTURE AND PATTERN WHICH INDICATES THAT STEREOGNOSIS IS INTACT. LOSS OF THIS ABILITY IS KNOWN AS
ASTEREOGNOSIS WHICH OCCURS IN LESIONS OF THE SUPERIOR PARIETAL LOBULE (OPTIONS B AND C) AND DORSAL
COLUMN PATHWAYS.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: APOCRINE GLANDS ARE PRESENT IN WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING?
questions.explanation:
APOCRINE GLANDS ARE PRESENT IN THE AXILLA.
362
EXOCRINE GLANDS CAN BE CLASSIFIED INTO THREE SUBTYPES, BASED ON THE MANNER IN WHICH THEIR
SECRETIONS ARE POURED OUT OF THE CELLS:
- APOCRINE
- MEROCRINE
- HOLOCRINE
IN APOCRINE GLANDS, THE APICAL PARTS OF THE CELLS ARE SHED OFF TO DISCHARGE THE SECRETION. EXAMPLES
OF APOCRINE GLANDS ARE :
- SECRETION OF MILK FAT BY MAMMARY GLANDS
- ATYPICAL SWEAT GLANDS IN THE AXILLA, PERIANAL REGION, PERIUMBILICAL SKIN, MONS PUBIS.
- CERUMINOUS GLANDS OF THE EXTERNAL AUDITORY MEATUS ARE MODIFIED APOCRINE GLANDS
APOCRINE GLANDS ARE LARGE GLANDS FOUND IN THE DERMIS OR SUBCUTANEOUS FAT. THEY ARE A TYPE OF
SWEAT GLAND. IT CONSISTS OF A BASAL SECRETORY COIL FOLLOWED BY A STRAIGHT DUCT THAT OPENS INTO
THE PILARY CANAL ABOVE THE DUCT OF THE SEBACEOUS GLAND. IN HAIRLESS SKIN, IT DIRECTLY OPENS ONTO THE
SKIN SURFACE.
APOCRINE ACTIVITY IS MINIMAL BEFORE PUBERTY, AFTER WHICH IT IS ANDROGEN-DEPENDENT AND RESPONSIVE
TO EMOTIONAL STIMULI. IT IS CONTROLLED BY ADRENERGIC NERVES AND IS SENSITIVE TO ADRENALINE AND
NORADRENALINE. THE SECRETION IS INITIALLY STERILE AND ODORLESS, BUT IT UNDERGOES BACTERIAL
DECOMPOSITION TO GENERATE ODOROUS AND MUSKY COMPOUNDS. OBSTRUCTION OF APOCRINE SWEAT DUCTS
AND ASSOCIATED UPPER HAIR FOLLICLES IN THE AXILLAE, BREAST AREOLAE, AND PUBIC REGION, MAINLY IN
WOMEN, IS THOUGHT TO CAUSE FOX–FORDYCE DISEASE. IT IS ALSO IMPLICATED IN THE CAUSATION OF A
PAINFUL, OCCASIONALLY DEBILITATING CONDITION CALLED HIDRADENITIS SUPPURATIVA.
THE GIVEN IMAGE SHOWS AN ILLUSTRATION OF APOCRINE SECRETION.
363

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt:
A STUDENT HAD HIS JAW LOCKED WHILE YAWNING. WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING MUSCLES IS ATTACHED TO THE
ARTICULAR DISC OF THE TEMPOROMANDIBULAR JOINT?
questions.explanation:
THE MUSCLE THAT IS ATTACHED TO THE ARTICULAR DISC OF THE TEMPOROMANDIBULAR JOINT IS THE LATERAL
PTERYGOID.
LATERAL PTERYGOID MUSCLE:
- ORIGIN - UPPER HEAD ARISES FROM THE INFRATEMPORAL SURFACE AND INFRATEMPORAL CREST OF THE GREATER
WING OF THE SPHENOID BONE. THE LOWER HEAD ARISES FROM THE LATERAL SURFACE OF THE LATERAL PTERYGOID
PLATE.
- INSERTION - IT IS INSERTED INTO THE PTERYGOID FOVEA, THE CAPSULE OF THE TEMPOROMANDIBULAR JOINT,
AND THE ARTICULAR DISC.
THE ACTION OF LATERAL PTERYGOID MUSCLE IS DEPRESSION, PROTRUSION, AND SIDE-TO-SIDE MOVEMENT OF THE
JAW.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: IDENTIFY THE STRUCTURE(S) IN THE FOLLOWING HISTOLOGICAL IMAGE.
questions.explanation:
THE ABOVE HISTOLOGY IMAGE SHOWS THE GLOMERULUS.
GLOMERULUS IS A ROUNDED TUFT OF ANASTOMOSING CAPILLARIES LINED BY FENESTRATED ENDOTHELIUM. BLOOD
ENTERS THE TUFT THROUGH AN AFFERENT ARTERIOLE AND LEAVES IT THROUGH AN EFFERENT ARTERIOLE. IT IS
SUPPORTED BY THE MESANGIUM CONTAINING MESANGIAL CELLS AND A NON-CELLULAR MESANGIAL MATRIX.
THE GLOMERULAR CAPILLARY WALL IS THE FILTERING MEMBRANE AND CONSISTS OF FENESTRATED ENDOTHELIAL
CELLS, BASEMENT MEMBRANE, AND VISCERAL EPITHELIAL CELLS CALLED PODOCYTES, WHICH CONTAIN FOOT
PROCESSES.
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW SHOWS THE HISTOLOGY OF THE GLOMERULUS.
OPTION A: LEYDIG CELLS, ALSO KNOWN AS INTERSTITIAL CELLS OF LEYDIG, ARE PRESENT IN THE INTERSTITIAL
CONNECTIVE BETWEEN SEMINIFEROUS TUBULES.
316
THE TESTIS CONTAINS NUMEROUS SEMINIFEROUS TUBULES SEPARATED BY CONNECTIVE TISSUE IN
BETWEEN. SEMINIFEROUS TUBULES ARE LINED BY SEVERAL SPERMATOGONIA CELLS, WHICH PRODUCE
SPERMATOZOA, AND SERTOLI (SUSTENTACULAR) CELLS, WHICH HAVE A SUPPORTIVE FUNCTION.
THE CONNECTIVE TISSUE IN BETWEEN THE TUBULES IS MADE UP OF LEYDIG CELLS, COLLAGEN FIBERS,
FIBROBLASTS, MACROPHAGES, MAST CELLS, BLOOD VESSELS, AND LYMPHATICS. LEYDIG CELLS ARE LARGE, ROUND,
OR POLYHEDRAL CELLS WITH ECCENTRIC NUCLEI. THEY ARE LIGHTLY STAINED AND OFTEN HAVE A FOAMY
APPEARANCE. THEY SECRETE TESTOSTERONE UPON STIMULATION BY LUTEINIZING HORMONE FROM THE ANTERIOR
PITUITARY.
THE IMAGE BELOW SHOWS SEMINIFEROUS TUBULES AND LEYDIG CELLS.
OPTION B: ISLETS OF LANGERHANS MAKES UP THE ENDOCRINE PART OF THE PANCREAS.
ISLETS ARE CHARACTERIZED BY SECRETORY CELLS SUPPORTED BY RETICULIN FIBERS AND CONTAIN NUMEROUS
FENESTRATED CAPILLARIES. THERE IS A DELICATE CAPSULE AROUND EACH ISLET. THE ISLET CELLS ARE PALER THAN
THE SURROUNDING EXOCRINE CELLS, AS THEY HAVE LESS ROUGH ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM.
THE ISLET OF LANGERHANS IS MAINLY COMPOSED OF THREE TYPES OF CELLS:
- α OR A CELLS - LOCATED PERIPHERALLY AND SECRETE GLUCAGON
- β OR B CELLS - LOCATED CENTRALLY AND PRODUCE INSULIN
- δ OR D CELLS - SCATTERED BETWEEN BETA CELLS AND SECRETE SOMATOSTATIN
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW SHOWS THE ISLETS OF LANGERHANS.
317
OPTION C: HASSALL'S CORPUSCLES ARE SMALL ROUNDED STRUCTURES PRESENT IN THE MEDULLA OF THE THYMUS.
EACH CORPUSCLE HAS A CENTRAL CORE OF DEGENERATED EPITHELIAL CELLS AND MACROPHAGES SURROUNDED BY
CONCENTRICALLY ARRANGED EPITHELIAL CELLS. THE DEGENERATED CELLS ULTIMATELY GIVE PINK STAINING HYALINE
MASS. THE FUNCTION OF THE CORPUSCLES OF HASSALL IS STILL NOT KNOWN.
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW SHOWS HASSALL'S CORPUSCLE.

THE SITE MARKED AS '3' IN THE X-RAY GIVEN ABOVE IS THE NECK OF THE FIBULA. INJURY AT THIS SITE CAUSES
FAILURE OF DORSIFLEXION (FOOT DROP) DUE TO INJURY TO THE COMMON FIBULAR NERVE (ALSO KNOW AS
COMMON PERONEAL NERVE)

THE COMMON FIBULAR NERVE IS DERIVED FROM THE DORSAL BRANCHES OF THE 4TH AND 5TH LUMBAR AND 1ST
AND 2ND SACRAL VENTRAL RAMI. IT RUNS OBLIQUELY ALONG THE LATERAL SIDE OF THE POPLITEAL FOSSA TO THE
FIBULAR HEAD. IT LIES BETWEEN THE BICEPS FEMORIS AND THE LATERAL HEAD OF THE GASTROCNEMIUS. IT THEN
CURVES LATERALLY AROUND THE NECK OF THE FIBULA AND GETS DIVIDED INTO SUPERFICIAL AND DEEP FIBULAR
NERVES.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: A DEFECT IN WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING AORTIC ARCHES CAUSES THE DEFECT SHOWN IN THE IMAGE?
questions.explanation:
THE IMAGE ABOVE SHOWS A PATENT DUCTUS ARTERIOSUS DUE TO A DEFECT IN THE LEFT SIDE OF THE 6TH AORTIC
ARCH.
USUALLY, IN TERM INFANTS, THE DUCTUS ARTERIOSUS CLOSES WITHIN 72 HOURS OF BIRTH. FAILURE OF THE
DUCTUS ARTERIOSUS TO CLOSE RESULTS IN PATENT DUCTUS ARTERIOSUS (PDA).
PDA USUALLY PRESENTS WITH A HYPERDYNAMIC PRECORDIUM, BOUNDING PERIPHERAL PULSES, WIDE PULSE
PRESSURE, A MACHINE-LIKE CONTINUOUS OR SYSTOLIC MURMUR, CARDIOMEGALY, INCREASED PULMONARY
VASCULAR MARKINGS, HEPATOMEGALY, INCREASING OXYGEN DEPENDENCE, CARBON DIOXIDE RETENTION, AND
RENAL FAILURE.
IN A MAJORITY OF CASES, PDA CLOSES SPONTANEOUSLY. IF SPONTANEOUS CLOSURE FAILS TO OCCUR, COX
INHIBITORS LIKE INDOMETHACIN OR IBUPROFEN CAN BE USED. SURGICAL LIGATION IS INDICATED IN CASE OF
CONTRAINDICATIONS TO MEDICAL MANAGEMENT OR FAILURE OF THE SAME.
OTHER OPTIONS
OPTION A: THE 4TH RIGHT AORTIC ARCH GIVES RISE TO THE PROXIMAL PART OF THE RIGHT SUBCLAVIAN ARTERY.
OPTION B: THE 4TH LEFT AORTIC ARCH GIVES RISE TO THE ARCH OF THE AORTA. DEFECTS INVOLVING THE 4TH LEFT
AORTIC ARCH COULD CAUSE A VARIETY OF AORTIC ARCH ANOMALIES, SUCH AS INTERRUPTION OF THE AORTIC ARCH,
BUT NOT PDA.
OPTION C: THE 6TH RIGHT AORTIC ARCH FORMS THE PROXIMAL PART OF THE RIGHT PULMONARY ARTERY.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTS WITH SWELLING UNDER THE LEFT EAR LOBULE AND COMPLAINS OF PAIN. WHICH OF THE
FOLLOWING STRUCTURES IS THE LIKELY CAUSE OF THE PAIN?
options:
INVESTING LAYER OF DEEP CERVICAL FASCIA

Answer Key
Question No. Correct Option
questions.explanation:
THE CAUSE OF THE PAIN IN THIS PATIENT COMPLAINING OF PAIN IN THE PAROTID REGION IS LIKELY TO BE THE
GREATER AURICULAR NERVE.
THE GREATER AURICULAR NERVE PROVIDES SENSORY INNERVATION TO THE SKIN OVERLYING THE PAROTID GLAND
AND THE EAR LOBULE. PAIN ASSOCIATED WITH SWELLING AND INFLAMMATION IN THE PAROTID REGION COULD BE
TRANSMITTED THROUGH THE GREATER AURICULAR NERVE. THE PAROTID GLAND IS COVERED BY A PAROTID CAPSULE
THAT IS DERIVED FROM THE INVESTING LAYER OF DEEP CERVICAL FASCIA. ANY ACUTE INFLAMMATION OF THE
GLAND SUCH AS ACUTE SIALADENITIS RESULTS IN PAIN IN THE PREAURICULAR REGION. THE PAIN IS MAINLY DUE
TO STRETCHING OF THE CAPSULE RESULTING IN STIMULATION OF THE GREATER AURICULAR NERVE.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: THE FACIAL NERVE IS NOT THE PRIMARY CAUSE OF PAIN IN THE PAROTID REGION DUE TO SWELLING.
THE HITZELBERGER SIGN(NUMBNESS IN THE POSTEROSUPERIOR MEATAL WALL OF THE EXTERNAL AUDITORY
CANAL), ASSOCIATED WITH FACIAL NERVE INVOLVEMENT, IS SEEN IN ACOUSTIC NEUROMA AND IS NOT THE CAUSE
OF PAIN IN THIS SCENARIO.
OPTION D: INVESTING LAYER OF DEEP CERVICAL FASCIA IS NOT THE CORRECT ANSWER BECAUSE THE INVESTING
LAYER OF DEEP CERVICAL FASCIA ITSELF DOES NOT TRANSMIT PAIN SENSATION. THE INVESTING LAYER OF DEEP
CERVICAL FASCIA IS A LAYER OF CONNECTIVE TISSUE THAT ENVELOPS THE NECK AND EXTENDS TO COVER THE
PAROTID GLAND, FORMING THE PAROTID CAPSULE. WHILE INFLAMMATION OR SWELLING IN THE PAROTID GLAND
CAN STRETCH THE CAPSULE AND CAUSE PAIN, THE ACTUAL TRANSMISSION OF PAIN SENSATION IS MEDIATED BY
SENSORY NERVES, SUCH AS THE GREATER AURICULAR NERVE, WHICH INNERVATES THE SKIN OVER THE PAROTID
GLAND AND THE EAR LOBULE.
THE GREATER AURICULAR NERVE (OPTION B) IS A MORE APPROPRIATE ANSWER IN THIS CONTEXT, AS IT IS
RESPONSIBLE FOR CARRYING THE PAIN SENSATION FROM THE AREA OF SWELLING AND INFLAMMATION IN THE
PAROTID REGION.
OPTION C: THE AURICULOTEMPORAL NERVE CAN CAUSE REFERRED PAIN DUE TO CARIES TOOTH, ULCERATIVE
LESIONS OF THE ORAL CAVITY, TEMPOROMANDIBULAR JOINT DISORDERS, AND SPHENOPALATINE NEURALGIA.
HOWEVER, IT IS NOT THE PRIMARY CAUSE OF PAIN IN THE PAROTID REGION DUE TO SWELLING.
322

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt:
THE SPINAL SENSORY NUCLEUS OF THE TRIGEMINAL NERVE HAS 2ND ORDER NEURONS TO CARRY WHICH
SENSATION?
questions.explanation:
THE TRIGEMINAL NERVE (CRANIAL NERVE V) IS RESPONSIBLE FOR SENSORY INPUT FROM THE FACE, AS WELL AS
MOTOR FUNCTIONS SUCH AS CHEWING. ITS SENSORY PATHWAY INVOLVES THREE BRANCHES: THE OPHTHALMIC
(V1), MAXILLARY (V2), AND MANDIBULAR (V3) DIVISIONS. THE FIRST-ORDER NEURONS FOR EACH DIVISION
ORIGINATE FROM DIFFERENT SENSORY GANGLIA:
1.OPHTHALMIC DIVISION (V1):
FIRST-ORDER NEURONS: CELL BODIES ARE LOCATED IN THE TRIGEMINAL GANGLION (ALSO CALLED THE SEMILUNAR
OR GASSERIAN GANGLION).
2. MAXILLARY DIVISION (V2):
FIRST-ORDER NEURONS: CELL BODIES ARE LOCATED IN THE TRIGEMINAL GANGLION.
3. MANDIBULAR DIVISION (V3):
FIRST-ORDER NEURONS: CELL BODIES ARE LOCATED IN THE TRIGEMINAL GANGLION.
378
THESE FIRST-ORDER NEURONS CARRY SENSORY INFORMATION FROM THE FACE TO THE BRAINSTEM. UPON
ENTERING THE BRAINSTEM, THE FIBERS SYNAPSE WITH SECOND-ORDER NEURONS IN SPECIFIC NUCLEI:
1. PRINCIPAL SENSORY NUCLEUS (MAIN SENSORY NUCLEUS):
A.RECEIVES INPUT FROM ALL THREE DIVISIONS OF THE TRIGEMINAL NERVE.
B.LOCATED IN THE PONS.
C.SECOND-ORDER NEURONS HERE CARRY DISCRIMINATIVE TOUCH AND PROPRIOCEPTIVE INFORMATION.
2. SPINAL TRIGEMINAL NUCLEUS (SPINAL NUCLEUS OF TRIGEMINAL):
A.RECEIVES INPUT MAINLY FROM THE MAXILLARY AND MANDIBULAR DIVISIONS.
B.LOCATED IN THE MEDULLA.
C.SECOND-ORDER NEURONS HERE CARRY PAIN AND TEMPERATURE SENSATIONS.
AFTER SYNAPSING IN THESE NUCLEI, THE SENSORY INFORMATION IS FURTHER RELAYED TO HIGHER BRAIN CENTERS
FOR PROCESSING AND PERCEPTION.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS NOT SEEN IN THE FLOOR OF THE INFERIOR HORN OF THE LATERAL VENTRICLE?
questions.explanation:
THE TAIL OF THE CAUDATE NUCLEUS IS NOT SEEN ON THE FLOOR OF THE INFERIOR HORN OF THE LATERAL VENTRICLE.
IT IS PRESENT ON THE ROOF OF THE INFERIOR HORN OF THE LATERAL VENTRICLE.
THE INFERIOR HORN IS THE LARGEST COMPARTMENT OF THE LATERAL VENTRICLE AND EXTENDS UP TO 2.5 CM
FROM THE TEMPORAL POLE. THE RELATIONS ARE:
ROOF - TAPETUM OF CORPUS CALLOSUM LATERALLY AND TAIL OF CAUDATE NUCLEUS MEDIALLY.
FLOOR (LATERAL TO MEDIAL) - COLLATERAL EMINENCE PRODUCED BY COLLATERAL FISSURE, HIPPOCAMPUS.
THE FLOOR OF THE TEMPORAL HORN CONSISTS OF THE HIPPOCAMPUS MEDIALLY AND THE COLLATERAL EMINENCE,
FORMED BY THE INFOLDING OF THE COLLATERAL SULCUS, LATERALLY. THE INFERIOR PART OF THE CHOROIDAL FISSURE,
LOCATED BETWEEN THE FIMBRIA OF THE FORNIX AND THE INFEROLATERAL ASPECT OF THE THALAMUS, LIES IN THE
MEDIAL WALL.
THE LATERAL VENTRICLE IS DIVIDED INTO THE BODY AND 3 HORNS. THE LOCATIONS OF THE PARTS ARE:
- BODY - PARIETAL LOBE
- ANTERIOR HORN - FRONTAL LOBE
- POSTERIOR HORN - OCCIPITAL LOBE
- INFERIOR HORN - TEMPORAL LOBE.
379
THE ANTERIOR HORN EXTENDS FROM THE GENU OF THE CORPUS CALLOSUM UP TO THE INTERVENTRICULAR
FORAMEN. THE RELATIONS OF THE ANTERIOR HORN ARE:
- ANTERIORLY - GENU AND ROSTRUM OF THE CORPUS CALLOSUM
- ROOF - ANTERIOR PART OF THE BODY OF THE CORPUS CALLOSUM
- FLOOR AND LATERAL WALL - CAUDATE NUCLEUS
- MEDIAL WALL - SEPTUM PELLUCIDUM AND ANTERIOR COLUMN OF FORNIX
THE BODY OR CENTRAL PART EXTENDS FROM THE INTERVENTRICULAR FORAMEN TO THE SPLENIUM OF THE CORPUS
CALLOSUM. THE RELATIONS OF THE BODY ARE:
- ROOF - BODY OF THE CORPUS CALLOSUM
- MEDIAL WALL - SEPTUM PELLUCIDUM
- FLOOR (FROM LATERAL TO MEDIAL) - CAUDATE NUCLEUS, STRIA TERMINALIS, THALAMOSTRIATE VEIN, THALAMUS,
CHOROID PLEXUS, AND BODY OF THE FORNIX
THE POSTERIOR HORN EXTENDS FROM THE SPLENIUM TO THE OCCIPITAL POLE. THE RELATIONS ARE:
- ROOF AND LATERAL WALL - TAPETUM OF CORPUS CALLOSUM
- MEDIAL WALL - FORCEPS MAJOR AND CALCAR AVIS (CALCARINE SULCUS
NOTE: THERE IS NO LATERAL WALL FOR THE LATERAL VENTRICLE.
380

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING MARKED AREAS IN THE HISTOPATHOLOGICAL SPECIMEN SHOWS CALCIFICATION?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN SPECIMEN IS THAT OF AN EPIPHYSEAL CARTILAGE, WHERE ZONE 3 CORRESPONDS TO THE ZONE OF
CALCIFICATION.
EPIPHYSEAL CARTILAGE IS DIVIDED INTO FIVE ZONES :
- THE RESTING ZONE CONSISTS OF HYALINE CARTILAGE WITHOUT MORPHOLOGICAL CHANGES IN THE CELLS (OPTION
1)
- IN THE PROLIFERATIVE ZONE, CHONDROCYTES DIVIDE RAPIDLY AND FORM COLUMNS OF STACKED CELLS PARALLEL
TO THE LONG AXIS OF THE BONE (OPTION 2)
- THE HYPERTROPHIC CARTILAGE ZONE CONTAINS LARGE CHONDROCYTES WHOSE CYTOPLASM HAS ACCUMULATED
GLYCOGEN. THE RESORBED MATRIX IS REDUCED TO THIN SEPTA BETWEEN THE CHONDROCYTES.
- SIMULTANEOUS WITH THE DEATH OF CHONDROCYTES IN THE CALCIFIED CARTILAGE ZONE, THE THIN SEPTA OF
CARTILAGE MATRIX BECOME CALCIFIED BY THE DEPOSIT OF HYDROXYAPATITE.
- IN THE OSSIFICATION ZONE, ENDOCHONDRAL BONE TISSUE APPEARS (OPTION 4). BLOOD CAPILLARIES AND
OSTEOPROGENITOR CELLS FORMED BY MITOSIS OF CELLS ORIGINATING FROM THE PERIOSTEUM INVADE THE
CAVITIES LEFT BY THE CHONDROCYTES. THE OSTEOPROGENITOR CELLS FORM OSTEOBLASTS, WHICH ARE DISTRIBUTED
IN A DISCONTINUOUS LAYER OVER THE SEPTA OF THE CALCIFIED CARTILAGE MATRIX. ULTIMATELY, THE OSTEOBLASTS
DEPOSIT BONE MATRIX OVER THE THREE-DIMENSIONAL CALCIFIED CARTILAGE MATRIX.
THE EPIPHYSEAL CARTILAGE IS RESPONSIBLE FOR THE GROWTH IN THE LENGTH OF BONE AND IT DISAPPEARS IN
ADULTS, WHICH IS WHY BONE GROWTH CEASES IN ADULTHOOD.
381

THE STRUCTURES PASSING IN BETWEEN THE SUPERIOR CONSTRICTOR MUSCLE ( STRUCTURE 1 ) AND MIDDLE
CONSTRICTOR MUSCLE ( STRUCTURE 2) ARE GLOSSOPHARYNGEAL NERVE AND STYLOPHARYNGEUS MUSCLE.
THE STRUCTURES PASSING IN BETWEEN PHARYNGEAL MUSCLES ARE AS FOLLOWS:
1. SINUS OF MORGAGNI - IT IS A SEMILUNAR SPACE THAT EXISTS BETWEEN THE UPPER CONCAVE BORDER OF THE
SUPERIOR CONSTRICTOR AND THE SKULL BASE. IT IS CLOSED OFF BY THE UPPER STURDY PORTION OF THE
PHARYNGOBASILAR FASCIA. STRUCTURES PASSING THROUGH THIS SPACE INCLUDE:
A. THE AUDITORY TUBE
B. THE LEVATOR VELI PALATINI MUSCLE (OPTION C)
C. THE ASCENDING PALATINE ARTERY
382

2. BETWEEN THE SUPERIOR AND MIDDLE CONSTRICTORS - THE STYLOPHARYNGEUS MUSCLE AND THE
GLOSSOPHARYNGEAL NERVE.
3. BETWEEN THE MIDDLE AND INFERIOR CONSTRICTORS -THE INTERNAL LARYNGEAL NERVE AND THE SUPERIOR
LARYNGEAL VESSELS PENETRATE THE THYROHYOID MEMBRANE (OPTION B).
4. BETWEEN THE LOWER BORDER OF THE INFERIOR CONSTRICTOR AND THE ESOPHAGUS - THE RECURRENT

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt:
AT WHAT VERTEBRAL LEVEL DOES THE PART MARKED IN THE IMAGE LIE IN A NORMAL ANATOMICAL
POSITION?
options: DISC SPACE BETWEEN L4 AND L5
questions.explanation:
IN THE RIGHT PELVIC BONE GIVEN ABOVE THE MARKED STRUCTURE IS THE ISCHIAL SPINE WHICH LIES
APPROXIMATELY AT THE LEVEL OF THE FIFTH SACRAL VERTEBRAE IN A NORMAL ANATOMICAL POSITION. AS THE TIP
OF THE COCCYX IS THE CLOSEST OPTION RELATING TO THE SPINE , IT CAN BE THE MOST APPROPRIATE ANSWER.
THE ISCHIAL SPINE IS A BONY PROMINENCE FOUND ON THE ISCHIUM, ONE OF THE THREE BONES THAT MAKE UP
THE HIP BONE. THE ISCHIAL SPINE FORMS A PART OF THE PLANE OF LEAST PELVIC DIMENSIONS OR NARROW
PELVIC PLANE WHICH COMPRISES OF :
- LOWER BORDER OF THE SYMPHYSIS PUBIS
- THE TIP OF ISCHIAL SPINES
- FIFTH SACRAL VERTEBRA
THE INTERSPINOUS DISTANCE IS THE DISTANCE BETWEEN THE TIP OF TWO ISCHIAL SPINES. ( BISPINOUS
DIAMETER = 10.5 CM OR 4.5" )
THE IMPORTANT EVENTS OCCURRING AT THE NARROWEST PLANE IN THE PELVIS :
- IT CORRESPONDS ROUGHLY TO THE ORIGIN OF LEVATOR ANI MUSCLES.
- THE INTERNAL ROTATION OF THE FETAL HEAD OCCURS DURING LABOUR AT THIS PLANE.
- IT MARKS THE BEGINNING OF THE FORWARD CURVE OF THE PELVIC AXIS
- THIS LEVEL OF ISCHIAL SPINES INDICATES STATION ‘O’
- WHEN THE FETAL HEAD STATION IS AT ‘O’, THE HEAD IS CONSIDERED TO BE ENGAGED.
- DEEP TRANSVERSE ARREST OCCURS AT THIS PLANE.
- THE ISCHIAL SPINE CAN SERVE AS A LANDMARK IN PUDENDAL ANAESTHESIA, AS THE PUDENDAL NERVE LIES
CLOSE TO THE ISCHIAL SPINE
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW HIGHLIGHTS THE INTERSPINOUS DISTANCE SEEN THROUGH THE PELVIC INLET.
383

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: THE NERVE RELATED TO THE AREA MARKED IN THE PICTURE HAS ITS ROOT VALUE FROM?
options: DORSAL ROOT GANGLIA OF T1 AND T2
questions.explanation:
THE ABOVE IS AN IMAGE OF THE LEFT LUNG WITH THE ARROW POINTING AT THE NERVE PASSING ANTERIOR TO THE
LEFT HILUM. THE PHRENIC NERVE PASSES IN FRONT OF THE LEFT HILUM AND HAS ITS ROOT VALUE FROM THE
VENTRAL HORN OF C4.
IN THE GIVEN IMAGE, THE LEFT LUNG IS IDENTIFIED BY THE VERTICAL SEQUENCE OF STRUCTURES AT THE LEFT
HILUM - PULMONARY ARTERY, PRINCIPAL (HYPARTERIAL) BRONCHUS, AND INFERIOR PULMONARY VEIN. THE
IMAGE ALSO SHOWS AN OBLIQUE FISSURE DIVIDING THE LUNG INTO SUPERIOR AND INFERIOR LOBES.
THE PHRENIC NERVE, ORIGINATING FROM THE CERVICAL NERVES C3–C5, IS A MIXED NERVE THAT CARRIES MOTOR
FIBRES TO THE DIAPHRAGM AND SENSORY FIBRES FROM THE MEDIASTINAL PLEURA, PERICARDIUM, AND A
PORTION OF THE PERITONEUM.
THE COURSE OF THE LEFT PHRENIC NERVE:
384
CERVICAL REGION - BOTH PHRENIC NERVES PASS, ANTERIOR TO SCALENUS ANTERIOR MUSCLE
POSTERIOR TO STERNOCLEIDOMASTOID AND INFERIOR BELLY OF OMOHYOID
POSTERIOR TO INTERNAL JUGULAR VEIN, TRANSVERSE CERVICAL ARTERY, AND SUPRASCAPULAR ARTERY
POSTERIOR TO THE THORACIC DUCT ON THE LEFT
ROOT OF THE NECK - IT LIES MEDIAL TO THE TRUNKS OF THE BRACHIAL PLEXUS IN THE NECK. AT THE ROOT OF THE
NECK, IT RUNS ANTERIOR TO THE SECOND PART OF THE SUBCLAVIAN ARTERY AND POSTERIOR TO THE SUBCLAVIAN
VEIN.
THORAX - THE PHRENIC NERVE ENTERS THE THORAX BY CROSSING MEDIALLY IN FRONT OF THE INTERNAL THORACIC
ARTERY. WITHIN THE THORAX, THE PHRENIC NERVE DESCENDS ANTERIOR TO THE PULMONARY HILUM BETWEEN
THE FIBROUS PERICARDIUM AND MEDIASTINAL PLEURA, ACCOMPANIED BY THE PERICARDIACOPHRENIC VESSELS.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt:
THE STRUCTURE MARKED AS 'X' IN IMAGE A HAS A DIRECT CONNECTION WITH WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING
STRUCTURES MARKED IN IMAGE B?
questions.explanation:
IMAGE A SHOWS A SECTION OF THE CEREBELLUM AND IMAGE B SHOWS A SECTION OF THE MIDBRAIN. THE
STRUCTURE LABELED AS 'X' REPRESENTS THE DENTATE NUCLEUS OF THE CEREBELLUM, WHICH HAS A DIRECT
CONNECTION WITH THE STRUCTURE MARKED AS '1', WHICH IS THE RED NUCLEUS.
THE DENTATE NUCLEUS IS THE LARGEST OF THE CEREBELLAR NUCLEI. IT HAS THE SHAPE OF A CRUMPLED BAG WITH
THE OPENING FACING MEDIALLY. THE INTERIOR OF THE BAG IS FILLED WITH WHITE MATTER MADE UP OF EFFERENT
FIBERS THAT LEAVE THE NUCLEUS THROUGH THE OPENING TO FORM A LARGE PART OF THE SUPERIOR CEREBELLAR
PEDUNCLE.
THE EFFERENT PATHWAYS FROM THE DENTATE NUCLEUS CONNECT TO THE THALAMUS AND THE RED NUCLEUS, VIA
THE DENTATO- RUBRO -THALAMIC PATHWAY.
OTHER STRUCTURES IN THE IMAGE B :
2 - REPRESENTS SUPERIOR COLLICULUS, WHICH RECEIVES AFFERENTS FROM THE RETINA AND THE OCCIPITAL
CORTEX.
3 - REPRESENTS SUBSTANTIA NIGRA, WHICH RECEIVES AFFERENTS MAINLY FROM THE CAUDATE NUCLEUS
4 - REPRESENTS THE CRUS CEREBRI, WHICH CONTAINS FIBERS FROM THE CEREBRAL CORTEX.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING STATEMENTS IS TRUE CONCERNING THE ANATOMY OF THE BREAST?
options: INNER QUADRANTS CONTAIN MOST BREAST TISSUE
LIGAMENTS OF COOPER ARE FOUND ONLY IN LOWER QUADRANTS
TAIL OF SPENCE EXTENDS ACROSS ANTERIOR AXILLARY FOLD
questions.answer: TAIL OF SPENCE EXTENDS ACROSS ANTERIOR AXILLARY FOLD
questions.explanation:
THE TAIL OF SPENCE EXTENDS ACROSS THE ANTERIOR AXILLARY FOLD AND IS A SMALL EXTENSION OF THE UPPER
LATERAL QUADRANT OF THE BREAST.
THE BREAST LIES IN THE SUPERFICIAL FASCIA OF THE PECTORAL REGION. IT IS DIVIDED INTO FOUR QUADRANTS, I.E.
UPPER MEDIAL, UPPER LATERAL, LOWER MEDIAL AND LOWER LATERAL.
VERTICALLY, IT EXTENDS FROM THE SECOND TO THE SIXTH RIBS. HORIZONTALLY, IT EXTENDS FROM THE LATERAL
BORDER OF THE STERNUM TO THE MIDAXILLARY LINE. A SMALL EXTENSION OF THE UPPER LATERAL QUADRANT,
CALLED THE AXILLARY TAIL OF SPENCE, PASSES THROUGH AN OPENING IN THE DEEP FASCIA AND LIES IN THE
AXILLA. THE OPENING IS CALLED THE FORAMEN OF LANGER.
387
THE BREAST LIES ON THE DEEP PECTORAL FASCIA COVERING THE PECTORALIS MAJOR AND SERRATUS ANTERIOR
SUPERIORLY, THE EXTERNAL ABDOMINAL OBLIQUE AND ITS APONEUROSIS INFERIORLY, AND THE CLAVIPECTORAL
FASCIA LATERALLY. FIBROUS STRANDS OR SHEETS CONSISTING OF CONDENSATIONS OF CONNECTIVE TISSUE EXTEND
BETWEEN THE POSTERIOR LAMINA OF THE SUPERFICIAL FASCIA AND THE DERMIS. THESE SUSPENSORY LIGAMENTS
(RETINACULA OR COOPER’S LIGAMENTS) ARE OFTEN WELL-DEVELOPED IN THE SUPERIOR PARTS OF THE BREAST AND
SUPPORT THE BREAST TISSUE, HELPING TO MINIMIZE DROOPING.
THE BREASTS NORMALLY COMPRISE UP TO 20 DISCRETE LOBES THAT CONTAIN DUCTAL-GLANDULAR TISSUE
CONSISTING OF BRANCHING DUCTS AND TERMINAL SECRETORY LOBULES IN A CONNECTIVE TISSUE STROMA. EACH
LOBE IS DERIVED BY BRANCHING FROM ONE CENTRAL LACTIFEROUS DUCT IN THE NIPPLE. THE TERMINAL DUCT
LOBULAR UNIT (TDLU OR LOBULE) IS THE FUNCTIONAL MILK SECRETORY COMPONENT OF THE BREAST.
THE UPPER OUTER QUADRANT OF THE BREAST CONTAINS A GREATER VOLUME OF TISSUE THAN THE OTHER
QUADRANTS. THIS IS THE REASON FOR THE MAJORITY OF THE CARCINOMAS ARISING IN THE UPPER OUTER
QUADRANT.
388

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt:
A PROFESSOR UNDERWENT A LEFT PAROTIDECTOMY. POST SURGERY SHE COMPLAINS OF LEFT LOWER LIP
PARALYSIS. WHICH STRUCTURE IS INVOLVED?
questions.explanation:
LOWER LIP PARALYSIS IS CAUSED BY DAMAGE TO THE CERVICAL BRANCH OF THE FACIAL NERVE.
THE CERVICAL BRANCH OF THE FACIAL NERVE IS RESPONSIBLE FOR INNERVATING THE PLATYSMA MUSCLE, WHICH IS
ONE OF THE MUSCLES INVOLVED IN THE MOVEMENTS OF THE LOWER LIP. DAMAGE TO THIS NERVE CAN
POTENTIALLY LEAD TO PARALYSIS OF THE LOWER LIP.
THE FACIAL NERVE IS THE MOTOR NERVE OF THE FACE. ITS FIVE TERMINAL BRANCHES EMERGE FROM THE PAROTID
GLAND AND DIVERGE TO SUPPLY THE VARIOUS FACIAL MUSCLES AS FOLLOWS :
- TEMPORAL — FRONTALIS, AURICULAR MUSCLES, ORBICULARIS OCULI
- ZYGOMATIC — ORBICULARIS OCULI (LOWER EYELID PART)
- BUCCAL — MUSCLES OF THE CHEEK AND UPPER LIP
- MARGINAL MANDIBULAR — MUSCLES OF THE LOWER LIP
- CERVICAL — PLATYSMA

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: IDENTIFY THE NORMAL ANATOMICAL VARIATION GIVEN IN THE FOLLOWING CT IMAGE.
questions.explanation:
THE CT FINDING IN THE IMAGE IS SUGGESTIVE OF AN ABERRANT RIGHT SUBCLAVIAN ARTERY.
AN ABERRANT RIGHT SUBCLAVIAN ARTERY OCCURS WHEN THE RIGHT FOURTH AORTIC ARCH AND RIGHT DORSAL AORTA
INVOLUTE CRANIAL TO THE SEVENTH INTERSEGMENTAL ARTERY.
THIS ARTERY ARISES DISTAL TO THE LEFT SUBCLAVIAN ARTERY AND CROSSES THE MIDLINE POSTERIOR TO THE
ESOPHAGUS. BECAUSE OF THE ABSENCE OF A NORMAL RIGHT SUBCLAVIAN-CAROTID JUNCTION TO PULL DOWN THE
RIGHT RECURRENT LARYNGEAL NERVE (RLN) DURING EMBRYOLOGIC DEVELOPMENT, THE RIGHT RLN FOLLOWS A
STRAIGHT PATH FROM THE VAGUS TO THE LARYNX AND IS CALLED A NON-RECURRENT RIGHT LARYNGEAL NERVE.
MOST PATIENTS WITH THIS ANOMALY ARE ASYMPTOMATIC, AND THE ABERRANT SUBCLAVIAN ARTERY IS OF NO
CLINICAL CONSEQUENCE. DYSPHAGIA CAUSED BY COMPRESSION OF THE ESOPHAGUS BY AN ABNORMAL
SUBCLAVIAN ARTERY IS CALLED DYSPHAGIA LUSORIA.
389

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: IDENTIFY THE MARKED STRUCTURE
questions.explanation:
THE MARKED STRUCTURE IS SUPERFICIAL TEMPORAL ARTERY.
THE SUPERFICIAL TEMPORAL ARTERY IS ONE OF THE TERMINAL BRANCHES OF THE EXTERNAL CAROTID ARTERY,
ALONG WITH THE MAXILLARY ARTERY. IT ASCENDS IN FRONT OF THE EAR, PASSING OVER THE ZYGOMATIC ARCH AND
TRAVELS SUPERFICIALLY, SUPPLYING THE SCALP AND AREAS AROUND THE TEMPLE.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: THE POSTERIOR AURICULAR ARTERY IS SMALLER AND LOCATED POSTERIOR TO THE EAR.
OPTION C: THE MIDDLE MENINGEAL ARTERY IS DEEP WITHIN THE CRANIAL CAVITY AND SUPPLIES THE
MENINGES.
OPTION D: THE OCCIPITAL ARTERY LIES POSTERIORLY AND SUPPLIES THE SCALP AT THE BACK OF THE HEAD.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: THE MARKED STRUCTURE SERVES AS A SURFACE LANDMARK FOR WHICH ANATOMICAL STRUCTURE?
questions.explanation:
THE MARKED STRUCTURE INDICATES THE PTERION AND IT SERVES AS A LANDMARK FOR THE STEM OF THE LATERAL
SULCUS.
THE FRONTAL, PARIETAL, TEMPORAL, AND SPHENOID BONES MEET AT THE PTERION. IT IS A LANDMARK FOR THE
STEM OF THE LATERAL SULCUS (SYLVIAN FISSURE), THE MOST PROMINENT SULCUS OF THE CEREBRAL HEMISPHERE.
IT SEPARATES THE FRONTAL LOBE FROM THE TEMPORAL LOBE. DEEP TO THE LATERAL SULCUS LIES THE INSULAR
CORTEX.
PTERION MARKS AS A SURFACE LANDMARK FOR THE FOLLOWING STRUCTURES:
- MIDDLE MENINGEAL ARTERY AND VEIN: FRACTURES IN THIS AREA CAN RUPTURE THE MIDDLE MENINGEAL
ARTERY, LEADING TO AN EPIDURAL HEMATOMA.
- BROCA’S AREA: LOCATED IN THE DOMINANT HEMISPHERE (USUALLY LEFT) IN THE INFERIOR FRONTAL GYRUS, IT
LIES IN PROXIMITY TO THE PTERION
- THE INSULAR CORTEX AND PARTS OF THE BASAL GANGLIA, SUCH AS THE PUTAMEN, ARE LOCATED DEEP TO THE
PTERION, BENEATH THE LATERAL SULCUS.
- STEM OF THE LATERAL SULCUS, ALSO CALLED THE SYLVIAN FISSURE. IT HOUSES THE MIDDLE CEREBRAL ARTERY AND
ITS BRANCHES, PLAYING A CRUCIAL ROLE IN BRAIN VASCULARIZATION AND CORTICAL ORGANIZATION.
DURING SURGERIES, THE PTERION IS A COMMON SITE FOR TREPHINING (MAKING A HOLE IN THE SKULL).
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: THE PINEAL GLAND IS LOCATED IN THE POSTERIOR ASPECT OF THE CRANIAL FOSSA IN THE BRAIN. IT IS
LOCATED DEEP IN THE BRAIN, NEAR THE MIDLINE.
OPTION B: WENICKE'S AREA IS IN THE SUPERIOR TEMPORAL GYRUS IN THE DOMINANT CEREBRAL HEMISPHERE.
IT IS FOUND IN THE POSTERIOR PART OF THE SUPERIOR TEMPORAL GYRUS.
391
OPTION D: THE INTERNAL CAROTID ARTERY SIPHON IS A PART OF THE INTERNAL CAROTID ARTERY'S COURSE.
CHARACTERIZED BY ITS S-SHAPED CURVATURE AS IT TRAVERSES THE CAVERNOUS SINUS AND ENTERS THE CRANIAL
CAVITY. THIS CONFIGURATION HELPS DISSIPATE PULSATILE ENERGY, REDUCING STRESS ON CEREBRAL VESSELS, AND
ALLOWS ADAPTABILITY TO CRANIAL MOVEMENTS WHILE MAINTAINING CEREBRAL PERFUSION.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt:
A 60-YEAR-OLD MALE RECOVERING FROM FACIAL NERVE PALSY COMPLAINS OF FOOD GETTING STUCK
BETWEEN THE CHEEK AND TEETH WHILE EATING. WHAT IS THE MUSCLE AFFECTED IN THIS CASE?
questions.explanation:
THIS PATIENT, RECOVERING FROM FACIAL NERVE PALSY, GETTING FOOD STUCK BETWEEN THE CHEEK AND TEETH
WHILE EATING, IS BECAUSE OF THE BUCCINATOR BEING AFFECTED.
THE BUCCINATOR IS A MUSCLE OF FACIAL EXPRESSION. IT IS INNERVATED BY THE FACIAL NERVE. IT IS KNOWN AS
THE WHISTLING MUSCLE.
THE BUCCINATOR MUSCLE IS PRIMARILY RESPONSIBLE FOR KEEPING FOOD BETWEEN THE TEETH DURING
MASTICATION BY PRESSING THE CHEEK AGAINST THE TEETH (INVOLVED IN FLATTENING THE CHEEKS AGAINST THE
GUMS AND TEETH).
IN FACIAL NERVE PALSY, PARALYSIS OF THE BUCCINATOR MUSCLE CAN LEAD TO FOOD ACCUMULATING IN THE
CHEEK POUCH, AS THE MUSCLE IS UNABLE TO CONTRACT PROPERLY.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: LEVATOR LABII SUPERIORIS: THIS MUSCLE ELEVATES THE UPPER LIP AND CONTRIBUTES TO FACIAL
EXPRESSIONS LIKE SHOWING THE UPPER TEETH AND DILATES THE NOSTRILS. IT IS NOT INVOLVED IN KEEPING FOOD
IN PLACE DURING CHEWING.
OPTION C : ZYGOMATICUS MAJOR: RESPONSIBLE FOR PULLING THE CORNER OF THE MOUTH UPWARD AND
OUTWARD, CONTRIBUTING TO SMILING. IT DOES NOT INFLUENCE FOOD PLACEMENT DURING MASTICATION.
OPTION D : ORBICULARIS ORIS: ENCIRCLES THE MOUTH AND HELPS IN CLOSING THE LIPS. WHILE IT IS INVOLVED
IN MASTICATION AND SPEECH, ITS PARALYSIS WOULD NOT CAUSE FOOD TO ACCUMULATE IN THE CHEEK.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS NOT A DERIVATIVE OF NEURAL CREST CELLS?
questions.explanation:
RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM IS NOT A DERIVATIVE OF NEURAL CREST CELLS.
RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM (RPE) IS DERIVED FROM THE NEUROECTODERM. THE RPE DEVELOPS FROM THE
OUTER LAYER OF THE OPTIC CUP, A STRUCTURE THAT ARISES FROM THE NEURAL TUBE (NEUROECTODERMAL ORIGIN),
NOT FROM NEURAL CREST CELLS.
NEURAL CREST CELLS ARE A GROUP OF CELLS THAT MIGRATE DURING EMBRYONIC DEVELOPMENT AND GIVE RISE TO
VARIOUS STRUCTURES, INCLUDING PARTS OF THE NERVOUS SYSTEM, FACE, AND HEART.
NEURAL CREST CELLS (NCC) ARE PRESENT ADJACENT TO THE NEURAL TUBE AND ARE SOMETIMES REFERRED TO AS
THE FOURTH GERM LAYER. IT CONTRIBUTES TO THE FORMATION OF MANY ORGANS AND TISSUES:
IN THE TRUNK REGION, THEY FORM:
- MELANOCYTES (OPTION D)
- SENSORY GANGLIA
- SYMPATHETIC AND ENTERIC NEURONS
392
- SCHWANN CELLS
- ADRENAL MEDULLA CELLS
IN THE CRANIAL REGION, THEY CONTRIBUTE TO THE:
- CRANIOFACIAL SKELETON
- NEURONS FOR CRANIAL GANGLIA-CILIARY GANGLION (OPTION C)
- CILIARY MUSCLES (OPTION A)
- SATELLITE GLIAL CELLS
- MELANOCYTES
SOME OF THE OTHER NEURAL CREST DERIVATIVES ARE:
- C CELLS OF THE THYROID GLAND
- CONOTRUNCAL SEPTUM IN THE HEART
- ODONTOBLASTS
- SMOOTH MUSCLE CELLS TO BLOOD VESSELS TO THE FACE AND FOREBRAIN.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: THE CRANIAL COMPONENT OF THE NEURAL CREST CELLS LEADS TO THE FORMATION OF?
questions.explanation:
THE CRANIAL COMPONENT OF NEURAL CREST CELLS (NCC) LEADS TO THE FORMATION OF CONOTRUNCAL SEPTUM.
THE CONOTRUNCAL SEPTUM IS ALSO KNOWN AS THE AORTOPULMONARY SEPTUM. THE FORMATION OF THE
AORTOPULMONARY SEPTUM IN THE TRUNCUS ARTERIOSUS DIVIDES THE OUTFLOW CHANNEL OF THE HEART INTO THE
VENTRAL AORTA AND THE PULMONARY TRUNK. PERSISTENT TRUNCUS ARTERIOSUS RESULTS WHEN THE CONOTRUNCAL
RIDGES FAIL TO FORM.
THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE HEART BEGINS IN THE THIRD WEEK OF EMBRYOGENESIS WITH THE FORMATION OF THE
CARDIOGENIC MESODERM. THE HEART TUBE FORMS THROUGH FUSION OF PAIRED ENDOCARDIAL TUBES, WHICH
THEN UNDERGO LOOPING AND SEPTATION TO ESTABLISH THE FOUR CHAMBERS. BY THE END OF THE EIGHTH WEEK,
THE HEART ACHIEVES ITS DEFINITIVE STRUCTURE, WITH SEPARATE ATRIA, VENTRICLES, AND MAJOR VESSELS.
THE HEART DEVELOPS FROM MESODERMAL ORIGINS, WITH DIFFERENT PARTS DERIVING FROM SPECIFIC
EMBRYONIC STRUCTURES:
- FIRST HEART FIELD (PRIMARY HEART FIELD): FORMS THE LEFT VENTRICLE AND PART OF THE ATRIA.
- SECOND HEART FIELD: CONTRIBUTES TO THE RIGHT VENTRICLE, OUTFLOW TRACT (CONUS ARTERIOSUS AND
TRUNCUS ARTERIOSUS), AND PART OF THE ATRIA.
- NEURAL CREST CELLS: CONTRIBUTE TO THE SEPTATION OF THE OUTFLOW TRACT AND THE FORMATION OF THE
AORTICOPULMONARY SEPTUM.
- PROEPICARDIUM (EPICARDIAL CELLS): FORMS THE EPICARDIUM AND CONTRIBUTES TO CORONARY VESSELS.
- SINUS VENOSUS: FORMS PART OF THE RIGHT ATRIUM (SINUS VENARUM) AND THE CORONARY SINUS.
- ENDOCARDIAL CUSHIONS: FORM THE ATRIOVENTRICULAR VALVES AND CONTRIBUTE TO SEPTATION.
OTHER OPTIONS:
393
OPTION A: SA NODE IS DERIVED FROM THE PRIMARY HEART FIELD - SINUS VENOSUS.
OPTION B: AV CUSHIONS ARE DERIVED FROM ADJACENT ENDOCARDIAL CELLS. THE ENDOCARDIAL CELLS ALONG
WITH THE EPICARDIUM AND MESENCHYME, FORM THE AV CUSHIONS.
OPTION D: CHORDAE TENDINEAE ARE FORMED FROM MESENCHYMAL TISSUE WITHIN THE HEART.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt:
A 15-YEAR-OLD BOY UNDERWENT SPLENECTOMY FOR IMMUNE THROMBOCYTOPENIC PURPURA. DURING THE
PROCEDURE, THE SURGEON NOTICED BLEEDING WHILE SEPARATING THE SPLEEN FROM THE STOMACH.
WHICH VESSELS ARE MOST LIKELY IMPLICATED IN THIS BLEEDING?
questions.explanation:
THIS PATIENT, UNDERGOING SPLENECTOMY, WHILE SEPARATING THE SPLEEN FROM THE STOMACH, IS LIKELY
BLEEDING FROM THE SHORT GASTRIC VESSELS.
IN AN OPEN SPLENECTOMY, THE GASTROSPLENIC LIGAMENT IS OPENED AND SHORT GASTRIC VESSELS ARE LIGATED
AND DIVIDED.
THE SPLEEN IS ATTACHED TO THE STOMACH THROUGH THE GASTROSPLENIC LIGAMENT. THE GASTROSPLENIC
LIGAMENT ATTACHES THE GREATER CURVATURE OF STOMACH TO THE UPPER POLE OF THE SPLEEN.
394
CONTENTS OF THE GASTROSPLENIC LIGAMENT INCLUDE:
- SHORT GASTRIC VESSELS
- LEFT GASTROEPIPLOIC VESSELS
HENCE, WHILE SEPARATING THE SPLEEN FROM THE STOMACH, THERE ARE MAXIMUM CHANCES OF BLEEDING IF
THERE IS INJURY TO THE SHORT GASTRIC VESSELS.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: LEFT GASTRIC VESSELS: LEFT GASTRIC VESSELS RUN ALONG THE LESSER CURVATURE OF THE STOMACH. IT
IS UNLIKELY TO BE THE SOURCE OF BLEEDING IN THIS CASE.
OPTION C: RIGHT GASTRO-EPIPLOIC VESSELS: THE RIGHT GASTROEPIPLOIC VESSELS RUN ALONG THE PYLORUS AND
INFERIOR REGION OF THE GREATER CURVATURE OF THE STOMACH. IT IS NOT A PART OF THE GASTROSPLENIC
LIGAMENT.
OPTION D: SPLENIC VESSELS: THE SPLENIC ARTERY AND VEIN RUN ALONG THE SUPERIOR BORDER OF THE
PANCREAS. THEY ARE NOT DIRECTLY INVOLVED IN THE SEPARATION OF THE SPLEEN FROM THE STOMACH.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: IDENTIFY THE MARKED STRUCTURE
questions.explanation:
THE MARKED STRUCTURE IS THE PRIMITIVE STREAK.
THE PRIMITIVE STREAK APPEARS IN THE EARLY STAGES OF GASTRULATION, A PROCESS THAT REORGANIZES THE
EPIBLAST INTO THREE GERM LAYERS: ECTODERM, MESODERM, AND ENDODERM. IT APPEARS AS A LINEAR
THICKENING ON THE DORSAL SURFACE OF THE EPIBLAST IN THE BILAMINAR EMBRYONIC DISC. IT IS FOUND IN THE
CAUDAL (TAIL-END) REGION OF THE DEVELOPING EMBRYO.
395
FUNCTIONS OF THE PRIMITIVE STREAK:
- SERVES AS THE SITE WHERE CELLS MIGRATE INWARD TO FORM THE MESODERM AND ENDODERM.
- MARKS THE BEGINNING OF GASTRULATION.
- DEFINES THE BODY AXIS (HEAD-TO-TAIL, LEFT-TO-RIGHT).
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: NOTOCHORD: A ROD-LIKE STRUCTURE DERIVED FROM MESODERM THAT FORMS AFTER THE PRIMITIVE
STREAK AND IS CRUCIAL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE NEURAL TUBE. LOCATED CRANIALLY RELATIVE TO THE
PRIMITIVE STREAK.
OPTION C: NEURAL GROOVE: A DEPRESSION IN THE ECTODERM THAT FORMS DURING NEURULATION, LEADING TO
THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE NEURAL TUBE. IT APPEARS AFTER THE PRIMITIVE STREAK.
OPTION D: SECONDARY NEURAL PLATE: PART OF THE NEURAL PLATE INVOLVED IN THE LATER STAGES OF NEURAL
TUBE DEVELOPMENT. IT IS NOT DIRECTLY RELATED TO THE PRIMITIVE STREAK.
396

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt:
WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS THE FIRST TO BE FORMED BY THE MIGRATION OF THE EPIBLAST ALONG THE
PRIMITIVE STREAK?
questions.explanation:
ENDODERM IS THE FIRST TO BE FORMED BY THE MIGRATION OF THE EPIBLAST ALONG THE PRIMITIVE STREAK.
GASTRULATION IS WHEN THE SINGLE-LAYERED BLASTULA REORGANIZES INTO A MULTI-LAYERED STRUCTURE CALLED
THE GASTRULA. THIS PROCESS ESTABLISHES THE THREE PRIMARY GERM LAYERS THAT GIVE RISE TO ALL TISSUES AND
ORGANS OF THE BODY. DURING GASTRULATION, EPIBLAST CELLS MIGRATE THROUGH THE PRIMITIVE STREAK TO
FORM THE THREE GERM LAYERS: ENDODERM, MESODERM, AND ECTODERM.
CELLS FROM THE EPIBLAST MIGRATE INWARD (INVAGINATION) THROUGH THE PRIMITIVE STREAK.
THE FIRST GROUP OF MIGRATING EPIBLAST CELLS REPLACES THE HYPOBLAST TO FORM THE DEFINITIVE ENDODERM.
THE ENDODERM GIVES RISE TO STRUCTURES LIKE THE GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT, LIVER, AND LUNGS.
SUBSEQUENT MIGRATING CELLS SPREAD BETWEEN THE EPIBLAST AND THE NEWLY FORMED ENDODERM TO CREATE
THE MESODERM, WHICH FORMS STRUCTURES LIKE MUSCLES, BONES, AND THE CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM.
REMAINING EPIBLAST CELLS THAT DO NOT MIGRATE THROUGH THE PRIMITIVE STREAK FORM THE ECTODERM,
WHICH GIVES RISE TO THE EPIDERMIS AND THE NERVOUS SYSTEM.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: CARDIAC MESODERM: THE MESODERM FORMS AFTER THE ENDODERM AND DIFFERENTIATES LATER
INTO SUBTYPES, INCLUDING THE CARDIAC MESODERM.
OPTION C: EPIDERMIS: THE EPIDERMIS ARISES FROM THE ECTODERM, WHICH FORMS AFTER BOTH THE
ENDODERM AND MESODERM.
OPTION D: NEURAL GROOVE: THE NEURAL GROOVE IS PART OF THE ECTODERM AND FORMS DURING
NEURULATION, WHICH OCCURS MUCH LATER THAN THE FORMATION OF THE ENDODERM.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt:
DURING WALKING, THE HIP BONE ON THE SIDE OF THE SUSPENDED LEG IS RAISED BY THE ACTION OF WHICH
MUSCLE PRESENT IN THE SUPPORTING LEG?
questions.explanation:
397
GLUTEUS MEDIUS OF THE SUPPORTING LEG IS RESPONSIBLE FOR RAISING THE HIP BONE ON THE SIDE OF THE
SUSPENDED LEG.
ACTIONS OF GLUTEUS MEDIUS:
- HIP ABDUCTION
- STABILIZES THE PELVIS DURING GAIT.
- ASSISTS THE INTERNAL ROTATION OF THE THIGH.
GLUTEUS MEDIUS AND GLUTEUS MINIMUS ACT AS THE ABDUCTORS OF THE HIP JOINT. STABILIZING THE PELVIS ON
THE FEMUR DURING WALKING IS DONE BY THESE MUSCLES. IT IS DEMONSTRATED BY ASKING THE SUBJECT TO
STAND ON ONE LIMB.
TRENDELENBURG SIGN:
TRENDELENBURG SIGN IS A CLINICAL SIGN USED TO ASSESS THE FUNCTION OF THE GLUTEUS MEDIUS.
IT IS POSITIVE WHEN THE PELVIS DROPS ON THE OPPOSITE SIDE OF THE STANCE LEG, INDICATING WEAKNESS OR
DYSFUNCTION OF THE GLUTEUS MEDIUS ON THE SUPPORTING LEG.
IN A HEALTHY INDIVIDUAL, THE GLUTEUS MEDIUS CONTRACTS TO PREVENT THE PELVIS FROM TILTING WHEN ONE
LEG IS LIFTED. IF THE GLUTEUS MEDIUS IS WEAK OR PARALYZED, THE PELVIS TILTS TOWARD THE SIDE OF THE
SUSPENDED LEG.
OPTION B: GLUTEUS MAXIMUS: EXTENDS AND EXTERNALLY ROTATES THE HIP; KEY FOR CLIMBING STAIRS AND
RISING FROM SITTING. WEAKNESS CAUSES DIFFICULTY IN HIP EXTENSION, AFFECTING ACTIVITIES LIKE STANDING
UP OR CLIMBING.
OPTION C: OBTURATOR INTERNUS: EXTERNALLY ROTATES AND STABILIZES THE HIP JOINT; ABDUCTS THE THIGH
WHEN THE HIP IS FLEXED. DYSFUNCTION CAN IMPAIR HIP ROTATION, COMMONLY AFFECTED IN PELVIC INJURIES.
OPTION D: QUADRATUS FEMORIS: EXTERNALLY ROTATES AND ADDUCTS THE HIP. INJURY OR ENTRAPMENT OF THE
NERVE TO QUADRATUS FEMORIS CAN CAUSE DEEP HIP PAIN AND WEAKNESS IN ROTATION.
398

OPTION B: THE ABDUCENS NERVE (CN VI) ALSO PASSES THROUGH THE CAVERNOUS SINUS AND SUPERIOR

OCULOMOTOR NERVE.
OPTION C: THE TROCHLEAR NERVE (CN IV) PASSES THROUGH THE SUPERIOR ORBITAL FISSURE AS WELL, BUT IT IS
THE SMALLEST CRANIAL NERVE AND FOLLOWS A HIGHER AND MORE LATERAL PATH THAN THE OCULOMOTOR NERVE.
OPTION D: THE OPHTHALMIC DIVISION OF THE TRIGEMINAL NERVE ENTERS THE LATERAL WALL OF THE CAVERNOUS
SINUS, BELOW THE OCULOMOTOR NERVE AND TROCHLEAR NERVE.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: AN ABSENT GAG REFLEX CAN RESULT FROM INJURY TO WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING NERVES?
questions.explanation:
AN ABSENT GAG REFLEX CAN RESULT FROM INJURY TO THE GLOSSOPHARYNGEAL NERVE (IX) AND THE VAGUS NERVE
(X).
THE AFFERENT NERVE FOR THE GAG REFLEX IS THE GLOSSOPHARYNGEAL NERVE, WHILE THE EFFERENT NERVE
CONSISTS OF BOTH THE GLOSSOPHARYNGEAL (TO THE STYLOPHARYNGEUS MUSCLE) AND VAGUS. BOTH THESE
NERVES PASS THROUGH THE JUGULAR FORAMEN AND DAMAGE TO THEM MAY BE THE CAUSE FOR LOSS OF GAG
REFLEX.
PHARYNGEAL BRANCHES OF THE GLOSSOPHARYNGEAL NERVE AND VAGUS NERVE FORM THE PHARYNGEAL PLEXUS
OF NERVES. THESE PLEXES MAINLY SUPPLY THE PHARYNX. IT ALSO HAS CONTRIBUTIONS FROM THE SUPERIOR
CERVICAL GANGLION.
NERVE SUPPLY BY THE PHARYNGEAL BRANCH OF THE VAGUS NERVE ARE:
- ALL THE MUSCLES OF THE SOFT PALATE(EXCEPT TENSOR VELI PALATINI - SUPPLIED BY MANDIBULAR DIVISION OF
THE TRIGEMINAL NERVE)
405
- ALL THE MUSCLES OF THE PHARYNX(EXCEPT THE STYLOPHARYNGEUS - SUPPLIED BY THE GLOSSOPHARYNGEAL
NERVE).
THE GLOSSOPHARYNGEAL NERVE IS RARELY DAMAGED ALONE. LESIONS WILL RESULT IN LOSS OF SENSATION OF THE
POSTERIOR THIRD OF THE TONGUE, REDUCED GAG REFLEX, LOSS OF SENSATION OVER THE IPSILATERAL SOFT PALATE,
ETC. MOTOR FIBRES TO THE STYLOPHARYNGEUS AND PARASYMPATHETIC SECRETOMOTOR FIBRES TO THE PAROTID
GLAND ARE ALSO SUPPLIED BY THE GLOSSOPHARYNGEAL NERVE. SENSORY SUPPLY INCLUDES UVULA, POSTERIOR
ONE-THIRD OF THE TONGUE, TYMPANIC CAVITY ETC.
THE MAIN FUNCTIONS OF IX AND X CAN BE TESTED TOGETHER BY ASSESSING SWALLOWING,
PHONATION/ARTICULATION AND SENSATION FROM THE PHARYNX/LARYNX.
GLOSSOPHARYNGEAL AND VAGUS NERVE EXAMINATIONS INCLUDE:
- OBSERVING THE POSITION AND SYMMETRY OF THE PALATE AND UVULA AT REST AND WITH PHONATION (“AAH”).
- BY ASSESSING THE STRENGTH OF THE COUGH

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt:
IF A TUMOR COMPRESSES THE STRUCTURES PASSING THROUGH THE OPENING MARKED IN THE GIVEN IMAGE,
WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING SENSATIONS WOULD BE AFFECTED?
options: SENSATION IN THE ANTERIOR SCALP AND DORSUM OF THE NOSE
questions.answer: SENSATION IN THE ANTERIOR SCALP AND DORSUM OF THE NOSE
questions.explanation:
THE MARKED FORAMEN IS THE SUPERIOR ORBITAL FISSURE. IF A TUMOUR COMPRESSES THE STRUCTURES PASSING
THROUGH THIS FORAMEN, IT WOULD IMPAIR SENSATION IN THE ANTERIOR SCALP AND DORSUM OF THE NOSE, AS
THIS WOULD AFFECT THE FRONTAL NERVE AND NASOCILIARY NERVE.
THE SUPERIOR ORBITAL FISSURE IS AN IMPORTANT ANATOMICAL OPENING IN THE SKULL THAT ALLOWS SEVERAL
CRITICAL STRUCTURES TO PASS THROUGH. AMONG THESE STRUCTURES, THE FRONTAL NERVE AND NASOCILIARY
NERVE ARE BRANCHES OF THE OPHTHALMIC NERVE, THE FIRST DIVISION OF THE TRIGEMINAL NERVE (CN V1),
WHICH IS RESPONSIBLE FOR SENSORY INNERVATION TO PARTS OF THE FACE.
THE FRONTAL NERVE PROVIDES SENSATION TO THE FOREHEAD, THE ANTERIOR SCALP, AND THE DORSUM OF THE
NOSE, WHILE THE NASOCILIARY NERVE SUPPLIES SENSATION TO PARTS OF THE NASAL CAVITY. THEREFORE, IF A
TUMOUR OR LESION COMPRESSES THE STRUCTURES PASSING THROUGH THE SUPERIOR ORBITAL FISSURE, IT WOULD
LIKELY AFFECT THE SENSATION IN THE ANTERIOR SCALP AND DORSUM OF THE NOSE BECAUSE THESE AREAS ARE
INNERVATED BY THE BRANCHES OF THE TRIGEMINAL NERVE THAT PASS THROUGH THIS FISSURE.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: SENSATION OF THE NASOPHARYNX IS INNERVATED BY OTHER BRANCHES OF THE TRIGEMINAL AND
GLOSSOPHARYNGEAL NERVE, NOT BY STRUCTURES PASSING THROUGH THE SUPERIOR ORBITAL FISSURE.
OPTION B: WHILE SOME SENSATION FROM THE NASAL CAVITY COMES FROM THE TRIGEMINAL NERVE, THE
SPECIFIC BRANCHES AFFECTED BY A LESION IN THE SUPERIOR ORBITAL FISSURE ARE MORE FOCUSED ON THE
ANTERIOR AREAS OF THE FACE.
OPTION D: SENSATION OF THE CHIN IS PRIMARILY INNERVATED BY THE MANDIBULAR BRANCH (CN V3) OF THE
TRIGEMINAL NERVE, WHICH PASSES THROUGH THE FORAMEN OVALE, NOT THE SUPERIOR ORBITAL FISSURE.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt:
A CHRONIC TOBACCO CONSUMER WENT TO THE DENTAL CLINIC WITH BLEEDING LESIONS ON HIS TONGUE AND
WAS DIAGNOSED WITH CARCINOMA OF THE TONGUE. WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING PAPILLAE, WHICH DO NOT
HAVE TASTE BUDS, IS LEAST LIKELY TO BE INVOLVED IN SUCH A CANCER?
questions.explanation:
AMONG THE DIFFERENT TYPES OF PAPILLAE ON THE TONGUE, THE ONE THAT DOES NOT HAVE TASTE BUDS IS THE
FILIFORM PAPILLAE.
406
FILIFORM PAPILLAE ARE MINUTE CYLINDRICAL OR CONICAL PROJECTIONS THAT ARE MAINLY PRESENT ON THE
DORSAL PART OF THE ANTERIOR 2/3RD OF THE TONGUE. THE FILIFORM PAPILLAE DO NOT CONTAIN TASTE BUDS.
THEY ARE COVERED BY KERATINIZED STRATIFIED SQUAMOUS EPITHELIUM.
OTHER PAPILLAE OF THE TONGUE ARE:
CIRCUMVALLATE PAPILLAE ARE 8-12 IN NUMBER WHICH ARE LARGE CYLINDRICAL STRUCTURES. THEY FORM A
V-SHAPED ROW JUST IN FRONT OF THE SULCUS TERMINALIS. USUALLY, THE ENTIRE PAPILLAE ARE COVERED BY
NON-KERATINIZED STRATIFIED SQUAMOUS EPITHELIUM. TASTE BUDS ARE PRESENT IN THE LATERAL WALL OF THESE
PAPILLAE WHICH SURROUNDS THE PAPILLAE CIRCUMFERENTIALLY.
FUNGIFORM PAPILLAE ARE LARGE, ROUNDED, AND RED AND ARE MAINLY PRESENT ON THE LINGUAL MARGINS AND
ALSO ON THE DORSAL SURFACE OF THE TONGUE. THEY ARE COVERED BY NON-KERATINIZED STRATIFIED SQUAMOUS
EPITHELIUM. THEY ARE SUPPLIED BY THE FACIAL NERVE.
FOLIATE PAPILLAE ARE RED, LEAF-LIKE MUCOSAL RIDGES THAT ARE PRESENT BILATERALLY IN TWO ZONES AT THE
SIDES OF THE TONGUE NEAR THE SULCUS TERMINALIS. THEY ARE COVERED BY NON-KERATINIZED STRATIFIED
SQUAMOUS EPITHELIUM.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt:
WHICH ARTERY IS USED FOR ARTERIOVENOUS SHUNTING WITH THE GREAT SAPHENOUS VEIN FOR
HEMODIALYSIS, AND IS LOCATED BEHIND THE MEDIAL MALLEOLUS AND 2.5 CM IN FRONT OF THE
TENDOCALCANEUS?
questions.explanation:
THE POSTERIOR TIBIAL ARTERY, LOCATED BEHIND THE MEDIAL MALLEOLUS AND 2.5 CM IN FRONT OF THE
TENDOCALCANEUS, THAT IS USED FOR ARTERIOVENOUS (AV) SHUNTING WITH THE GREAT SAPHENOUS VEIN FOR
HEMODIALYSIS.
THE POSTERIOR TIBIAL ARTERY IS SITUATED BEHIND THE MEDIAL MALLEOLUS AND APPROXIMATELY 2.5 CM IN
FRONT OF THE TENDOCALCANEUS, MAKING IT A SUITABLE SITE FOR CREATING AN AV FISTULA WITH THE GREAT
SAPHENOUS VEIN. THIS LOCATION ALLOWS FOR OPTIMAL ACCESS AND ENSURES THAT THE SHUNT CAN HANDLE THE
NECESSARY BLOOD FLOW FOR EFFECTIVE DIALYSIS WITH THE GREAT SAPHENOUS VEIN. HOWEVER, THEY ARE NOT
COMMONLY USED FOR AV SHUNTING IN COMMON PRACTICES.
ARTERIES USED FOR AV SHUNTING INCLUDE THE RADIAL ARTERY AND THE BRACHIAL ARTERY IN THE UPPER ARM,
WHICH ARE FREQUENTLY EMPLOYED FOR HEMODIALYSIS ACCESS. IN THE LOWER LEG, THE ANTERIOR TIBIAL ARTERY
AND THE PERONEAL (FIBULAR) ARTERY ARE LESS COMMONLY USED FOR THIS PROCEDURE.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: IN COMPARISON, THE ANTERIOR TIBIAL ARTERY IS LOCATED ON THE ANTERIOR ASPECT OF THE LEG AND
RUNS DOWN THE FRONT OF THE TIBIA, NOT BEHIND THE MEDIAL MALLEOLUS.
OPTION C: THE PERONEAL (FIBULAR) ARTERY IS SITUATED ON THE LATERAL SIDE OF THE LEG, TRAVELLING
ALONGSIDE THE FIBULA, AND IS ALSO NOT LOCATED BEHIND THE MEDIAL MALLEOLUS.
OPTION D: THE FIBULAR CIRCUMFLEX ARTERY IS A SMALL ARTERY AND IS NOT COMMONLY USED FOR
HEMODIALYSIS ACCESS. IT IS NOT A STANDARD CHOICE AND DOES NOT FIT THE ANATOMICAL LOCATION DESCRIBED,
AS IT IS A BRANCH OF THE ANTERIOR TIBIAL ARTERY.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: WHAT IS THE OUTER COVERING OF THE CONDITION SHOWN IN THE IMAGE?
questions.explanation:
THE DIAGNOSIS BASED ON THE GIVEN IMAGE IS OMPHALOCELE AND IS COVERED BY THE AMNION.
410
OMPHALOCELE IS A MIDLINE ABDOMINAL WALL DEFECT WHERE THE BOWEL AND OTHER SOLID VISCERA PROTRUDE
THROUGH THE UMBILICUS. IN THIS CONDITION, THE HERNIATED ORGANS ARE COVERED BY BOTH PERITONEUM
AND AN AMNION. THE UMBILICAL CORD INSERTS DIRECTLY INTO THIS SAC, WHICH HELPS IN IDENTIFYING THE
CONDITION. THE DEFECT OCCURS DUE TO THE FAILURE OF THE PHYSIOLOGICAL HERNIA TO RETURN TO THE BODY
CAVITY BY THE 11TH WEEK OF GESTATION.
THE SIZE OF AN OMPHALOCELE CAN VARY SIGNIFICANTLY. IT MAY BE RELATIVELY SMALL, CONTAINING ONLY THE
GUT, OR IT CAN BE CLASSIFIED AS A GIANT OMPHALOCELE IF IT MEASURES 4 CM OR MORE IN DIAMETER,
ENCOMPASSING THE GUT, LIVER, AND OTHER ABDOMINAL ORGANS. THE CONDITION IS OFTEN ASSOCIATED WITH
OTHER CONGENITAL ANOMALIES SUCH AS TRISOMIES 13, 15, 18, OR 21, BECKWITH-WIEDEMANN SYNDROME,
EXSTROPHY OF THE BLADDER OR CLOACA, AND PENTALOGY OF CANTRELL.
TREATMENT FOR OMPHALOCELE INVOLVES COVERING THE EXPOSED ORGANS TO PREVENT FLUID LOSS AND PROTECT
THEM FROM INFECTION. PROPHYLACTIC ANTIBIOTICS MAY BE ADMINISTERED IN CASE OF RUPTURE. SURGICAL
CORRECTION IS USUALLY PERFORMED ONCE THE BABY IS STABLE. IN OMPHALOCELE, SINCE THE UMBILICUS IS
COVERED BY A REFLECTION OF THE AMNION, THIS MEMBRANE ALSO COVERS THE OMPHALOCELE ITSELF,
DIFFERENTIATING IT FROM OTHER TYPES OF ABDOMINAL WALL DEFECTS.
NOTE : GASTROSCHISIS IS A CONDITION WHERE THE INTESTINAL LOOPS HERNIATE THROUGH THE DEFECT IN THE
ABDOMINAL WALL. THE DEFECT USUALLY LIES ON ONE SIDE OF THE UMBILICUS (RIGHT SIDE COMMONLY). THE
LOOPS OF THE BOWEL ARE NOT COVERED BY AMNION. IT IS ASSOCIATED WITH ELEVATED ALPHA-FETOPROTEIN
LEVELS.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: IDENTIFY THE MARKED STRUCTURE.
questions.explanation:
THE MARKED STRUCTURE IN THE IMAGE IS THE MEDIAL PECTORAL NERVE.
THE GIVEN IMAGE SHOWS THE MEDIAL PECTORAL NERVE ARISING FROM THE MEDIAL CORD OF THE BRACHIAL
PLEXUS. IT ALSO SHOWS THE AXILLARY ARTERY TRAVERSING INFERIOR TO THE MEDIAN PECTORAL NERVE AND THE
THORACOACROMIAL ARTERY. THE MEDIAL PECTORAL NERVE AND THE THORACOACROMIAL ARTERY BOTH CONTRIBUTE
TO THE NEUROVASCULAR SUPPLY OF THE PECTORAL MUSCLES.
411
AFTER ORIGINATING FROM THE MEDIAL CORD, THE MEDIAL PECTORAL NERVE PASSES ANTERIOR TO THE AXILLARY
ARTERY. THIS NERVE IS SPECIFICALLY KNOWN FOR ITS ANATOMICAL PATH OF PIERCING THE PECTORALIS MINOR
MUSCLE BEFORE BRANCHING OUT TO SUPPLY BOTH THE PECTORALIS MINOR AND THE PECTORALIS MAJOR
MUSCLES.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTS WITH SCIATICA AND TENDERNESS IN THE HAMSTRING MUSCLES. WHICH NERVE
SUPPLIES THE HYBRID MUSCLE THAT IS LIKELY TO BE SPARED IN THIS CONDITION?
questions.explanation:
THE ADDUCTOR MAGNUS IS THE HYBRID MUSCLE THAT IS LIKELY TO BE SPARED IN THIS CONDITION.
IN SCIATICA, THE SCIATIC NERVE IS TYPICALLY AFFECTED, WHICH BRANCHES INTO THE TIBIAL NERVE AND THE
COMMON PERONEAL NERVE. THE ADDUCTOR MAGNUS MUSCLE IS AN EXAMPLE OF A HYBRID MUSCLE WITH DUAL
INNERVATION:
- THE ADDUCTOR PART OF THE ADDUCTOR MAGNUS IS INNERVATED BY THE OBTURATOR NERVE.
- THE HAMSTRING PART OF THE ADDUCTOR MAGNUS IS INNERVATED BY THE TIBIAL NERVE.
DURING SCIATICA, THE TIBIAL NERVE IS OFTEN AFFECTED, WHICH WOULD IMPACT THE HAMSTRING PART OF THE
ADDUCTOR MAGNUS. HOWEVER, BECAUSE THE ADDUCTOR PART OF THE ADDUCTOR MAGNUS IS INNERVATED BY
THE OBTURATOR NERVE, IT REMAINS FUNCTIONAL AND IS LIKELY TO BE SPARED.
THE OBTURATOR NERVE ARISES FROM THE ANTERIOR DIVISION OF THE VENTRAL RAMI OF L2-L4. NEAR THE
OBTURATOR FORAMEN, IT DIVIDES INTO ANTERIOR AND POSTERIOR BRANCHES.
- ANTERIOR DIVISION SUPPLIES PECTINEUS, ADDUCTOR LONGUS, ADDUCTOR BREVIS, AND GRACILIS
- POSTERIOR DIVISION SUPPLIES ADDUCTOR MAGNUS, OBTURATOR EXTERNUS. IT ALSO SUPPLIES ADDUCTOR BREVIS
IF THE MUSCLE IS NOT SUPPLIED BY THE ANTERIOR DIVISION
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW SHOWS THE COURSE OF THE OBTURATOR NERVE.
412
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: THE COMMON PERONEAL NERVE IS A BRANCH OF THE SCIATIC NERVE AND CAN ALSO BE AFFECTED IN
SCIATICA. IT IS RESPONSIBLE FOR INNERVATING MUSCLES IN THE ANTERIOR AND LATERAL COMPARTMENTS OF THE
LEG.
OPTION B: THE TIBIAL NERVE IS A BRANCH OF THE SCIATIC NERVE AND IS OFTEN AFFECTED IN SCIATICA. IT
SUPPLIES THE HAMSTRING PART OF THE ADDUCTOR MAGNUS, WHICH WOULD BE IMPACTED DURING SCIATICA.
OPTION C: THE FEMORAL NERVE IS NOT INVOLVED IN SCIATICA. IT SUPPLIES THE QUADRICEPS AND OTHER
MUSCLES IN THE ANTERIOR COMPARTMENT OF THE THIGH, AND DOES NOT INNERVATE THE ADDUCTOR MAGNUS.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt: WHERE WILL YOU FIND THE EPITHELIUM SHOWN IN THE IMAGE?
questions.explanation:
THE EPITHELIUM SHOWN IN THE ABOVE IMAGE CAN BE FOUND IN THE URETER.
THE URETER IS LINED BY TRANSITIONAL EPITHELIUM (ALSO CALLED UROTHELIUM), SIMILAR TO THE URINARY
BLADDER. THIS SPECIALIZED EPITHELIUM ALLOWS STRETCHING, WHICH IS CRUCIAL AS THE URINE PASSES
THROUGH. THE PRESENCE OF TRANSITIONAL EPITHELIUM IS CHARACTERISTIC OF STRUCTURES IN THE URINARY
SYSTEM, SUCH AS THE URETERS, BLADDER, AND PART OF THE URETHRA.
GIVEN BELOW IS A CROSS-SECTION OF THE URETER SHOWING THE TRANSITIONAL EPITHELIUM AND THE LAYER OF
SMOOTH MUSCLE.
413
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: GALL BLADDER: THE GALL BLADDER IS LINED BY SIMPLE COLUMNAR EPITHELIUM, WHICH FACILITATES
THE ABSORPTION OF WATER AND ELECTROLYTES FROM BILE.
OPTION B: TRACHEA: THE TRACHEA IS LINED BY PSEUDOSTRATIFIED COLUMNAR CILIATED EPITHELIUM WITH
GOBLET CELLS, WHICH HELPS TRAP AND REMOVE PARTICLES FROM THE RESPIRATORY TRACT.
OPTION D: DUODENUM: THE DUODENUM IS LINED BY SIMPLE COLUMNAR EPITHELIUM WITH GOBLET CELLS,
AIDING IN DIGESTION AND NUTRIENT ABSORPTION.

DURING THE EXAMINATION OF A PATIENT, A PROFESSOR ASKS THE PATIENT TO INVERT HIS FOOT AND POINTS
TO A PROMINENT TENDON LOCATED BEHIND THE MEDIAL MALLEOLUS. WHICH TENDON IS BEING

THE TENDON BEING HIGHLIGHTED HERE IS OF THE TIBIALIS POSTERIOR.
IT PASSES BEHIND THE MEDIAL MALLEOLUS AND IS A KEY MUSCLE RESPONSIBLE FOR FOOT INVERSION. THE
TENDON OF THIS MUSCLE BECOMES PROMINENT IN THIS AREA DURING FOOT INVERSION. DYSFUNCTION OF THIS
TENDON CAN LEAD TO FLATFOOT DEFORMITY.

OPTION A: TIBIALIS ANTERIOR LIES ANTERIOR TO THE MEDIAL MALLEOLUS AND AIDS IN DORSIFLEXION AND

OPTION B: EXTENSOR DIGITORUM IS INVOLVED IN EXTENDING THE TOES AND RUNS ANTERIORLY TO THE FOOT, NOT

OPTION D: EXTENSOR HALLUCIS LONGUS EXTENDS THE BIG TOE AND RUNS ALONG THE ANTERIOR PORTION OF THE

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.prompt:
AN ELDERLY WOMAN REPORTS DIFFICULTY IN BUTTONING HER SHIRT AND INCREASED CLUMSINESS DURING
DAILY ACTIVITIES. ON EXAMINATION, SHE IS UNABLE TO MAKE AN 'O' SHAPE BY OPPOSING HER THUMB
AND INDEX FINGER. WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING MUSCLES IS MOST LIKELY INVOLVED?
options:
ABDUCTOR POLLICIS BREVIS
Answer Key
Question No. Correct Option
questions.answer:
ABDUCTOR POLLICIS BREVIS
Answer Key
Question No. Correct Option
questions.explanation:
THE DIFFICULTY IN BUTTONING THE SHIRT AND THE INABILITY TO MAKE THE "O" SHAPE WITH FINGERS SUGGEST
THE INVOLVEMENT OF THE ABDUCTOR POLLICIS BREVIS MUSCLE.
THIS IS A CASE OF ANTERIOR INTEROSSEOUS NERVE (AIN) SYNDROME. THE AIN IS A PURELY MOTOR BRANCH OF
THE MEDIAN NERVE THAT AFFECTS SPECIFIC MUSCLES IN THE FOREARM, THE FLEXOR POLLICIS LONGUS AND FLEXOR
DIGITORUM PROFUNDUS LEADING TO DIFFICULTY IN PERFORMING TASKS REQUIRING FINE MOTOR CONTROL, SUCH AS
THE "OK" SIGN. AMONG THE OPTIONS PROVIDED, THE ABDUCTOR POLLICIS BREVIS IS UNIQUELY AND
CONSISTENTLY INNERVATED BY THE RECURRENT MOTOR BRANCH OF THE MEDIAN NERVE, MAKING IT SUSCEPTIBLE
TO DYSFUNCTION IN CONDITIONS AFFECTING THE MEDIAN NERVE.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: THE OPPONENS POLLICIS IS INNERVATED PRIMARILY BY THE LATERAL TERMINAL BRANCH OF THE
MEDIAN NERVE, WITH SOME CONTRIBUTIONS FROM A BRANCH OF THE DEEP TERMINAL BRANCH OF THE ULNAR
NERVE. WHILE IT PLAYS A ROLE IN THUMB OPPOSITION, IT IS NOT CONSISTENTLY AFFECTED IN ANTERIOR
INTEROSSEOUS NERVE (AIN) SYNDROME, WHICH PRIMARILY IMPACTS DEEPER FLEXOR MUSCLES LIKE THE FLEXOR
POLLICIS LONGUS. THEREFORE, IT IS LESS LIKELY TO BE THE CAUSE OF THE PATIENT’S INABILITY TO PERFORM THE
"OK" SIGN.
OPTION B: THE PALMAR INTEROSSEI MUSCLES ARE INNERVATED BY THE DEEP BRANCH OF THE ULNAR NERVE.
BECAUSE THEY DO NOT RECEIVE ANY INNERVATION FROM THE MEDIAN NERVE, THEY ARE NOT IMPLICATED IN
415
AIN SYNDROME. THEIR PRIMARY FUNCTION INVOLVES THE ADDUCTION OF THE FINGERS.
OPTION C: THE FLEXOR POLLICIS BREVIS HAS DUAL INNERVATION: THE SUPERFICIAL HEAD IS SUPPLIED BY THE
RECURRENT BRANCH OF THE MEDIAN NERVE, WHILE THE DEEP HEAD IS INNERVATED BY THE DEEP BRANCH OF THE
ULNAR NERVE. THIS DUAL SUPPLY MAKES IT LESS LIKELY TO BE SOLELY AFFECTED IN AIN SYNDROME.
416

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.prompt:
ACCORDING TO MYOGENIC HYPOTHESIS OF RENAL AUTOREGULATION THE AFFERENT ARTERIOLES CONTRACT IN
RESPONSE TO STRETCH-INDUCED BY______
questions.explanation:
508
THE AFFERENT ARTERIOLES CONTRACT IN RESPONSE TO STRETCH INDUCED BY THE OPENING OF CALCIUM CHANNELS.
THE MECHANISM IS CALLED MYOGENIC AUTOREGULATION OF RENAL BLOOD FLOW AND GFR.
THE STRETCH OF THE VASCULAR WALL ALLOWS INCREASED MOVEMENT OF CALCIUM IONS FROM THE EXTRACELLULAR
FLUID INTO THE CELLS, CAUSING THEM TO CONTRACT. THIS CONTRACTION PREVENTS EXCESSIVE STRETCH OF THE
VESSEL. THIS PREVENTS EXCESSIVE INCREASE OF RENAL BLOOD FLOW AND GFR BY RAISING VASCULAR
RESISTANCE.
THIS MECHANISM MAY BE MORE IMPORTANT IN PROTECTING THE KIDNEY FROM HYPERTENSION-INDUCED
INJURY.
AUTOREGULATION HAS TWO MAIN MECHANISMS:
- METABOLIC MECHANISM: TISSUES PRODUCE VASODILATORY METABOLITES THAT REGULATE FLOW E.G.
PROSTAGLANDINS, NO, CO2, H+ AND K+
- MYOGENIC MECHANISM

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.prompt:
ACCORDING TO HERRINGTON CLASSIFICATION, THE DECEREBRATE RIGIDITY IS CHARACTERIZED BY ALL EXCEPT
______
options: RIGIDITY OCCURS IN ALL THE MUSCLES OF THE BODY
INCREASE IN THE RATE OF DISCHARGE OF THE ■ EFFERENT NEURON
INCREASED EXCITABILITY OF THE MOTOR NEURON POOL
DECEREBRATION PRODUCES NO PHENOMENON AKIN TO SPINAL SHOCK
questions.answer: RIGIDITY OCCURS IN ALL THE MUSCLES OF THE BODY
questions.explanation:
IN DECEREBRATE RIGIDITY, THERE IS RIGIDITY IN EXTENSOR MUSCLES OF ALL THE FOUR EXTREMITIES (NOT ALL
MUSCLES OF THE BODY).
DECEREBRATION
- COMPLETE TRANSECTION OF THE BRAIN STEM BETWEEN THE SUPERIOR AND INFERIOR COLLICULI PERMITS THE
BRAIN STEM PATHWAYS TO FUNCTION INDEPENDENTLY OF THEIR INPUT FROM HIGHER BRAIN STRUCTURES. THIS IS
CALLED A MID-COLLICULAR DECEREBRATION.
- THIS LESION INTERRUPTS ALL INPUT FROM THE CORTEX (CORTICOSPINAL AND CORTICOBULBAR TRACTS) AND RED
NUCLEUS (RUBROSPINAL TRACT), PRIMARILY TO DISTAL MUSCLES OF THE EXTREMITIES.
- THE EXCITATORY AND INHIBITORY RETICULOSPINAL PATHWAYS (PRIMARILY TO POSTURAL EXTENSOR MUSCLES)
REMAIN INTACT.
509
- THE DOMINANCE OF DRIVE FROM ASCENDING SENSORY PATHWAYS TO THE EXCITATORY RETICULOSPINAL
PATHWAY LEADS TO HYPERACTIVITY IN EXTENSOR MUSCLES IN ALL FOUR EXTREMITIES WHICH ARE CALLED
DECEREBRATE RIGIDITY.
- THE EXCITATORY INPUT FROM THE RETICULOSPINAL PATHWAY ACTIVATES γ-MOTOR NEURONS WHICH INDIRECTLY
ACTIVATE α-MOTOR NEURONS (VIA IA SPINDLE AFFERENT ACTIVITY). THIS IS CALLED THE GAMMA LOOP.
OPTION 4. SPINAL SHOCK IS DIFFERENT FROM DECEBRATE RIGIDITY AS IT IS A TRANSIENT STATE THAT CAN OCCUR
IMMEDIATELY AFTER A SPINAL CORD INJURY. IT IS CHARACTERIZED BY A TEMPORARY LOSS OR DEPRESSION OF
SPINAL REFLEXES BELOW THE LEVEL OF THE INJURY.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS TRUE FOR DECORTICATE RIGIDITY?
options: IT IS PRODUCED BY THE REMOVAL OF CEREBRAL CORTEX AND BASAL GANGLIA
FLEXION OF LOWER LIMBS AND EXTENSION OF UPPER LIMBS OCCURS
IT IS CHARACTERIZED BY FLEXION OF UPPER LIMBS AND EXTENSION OF LOWER LIMBS
questions.answer: IT IS CHARACTERIZED BY FLEXION OF UPPER LIMBS AND EXTENSION OF LOWER LIMBS
questions.explanation:
- REMOVAL OF THE CEREBRAL CORTEX (DECORTICATION) PRODUCES DECORTICATE RIGIDITY.
- CHARACTERIZED BY FLEXION OF THE UPPER EXTREMITIES AT THE ELBOW AND EXTENSOR HYPERACTIVITY IN THE
LOWER EXTREMITIES.
- THE FLEXION CAN BE EXPLAINED BY ACTIVE RUBROSPINAL EXCITATION OF FLEXOR MUSCLES IN THE UPPER
EXTREMITIES; THE HYPEREXTENSION OF LOWER EXTREMITIES IS DUE TO THE SAME CHANGES THAT OCCUR AFTER
MIDCOLLICULAR DECEREBRATION.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.prompt:
ACID CITRATE DEXTROSE (ACD), USED TO STORE BLOOD, PRESERVES THE RBCS FOR A PERIOD OF 21 DAYS.
THE STORAGE PERIOD WHEN ADDING PHOSPHATE ALONE AND WHEN ADDING ADENINE AND PHOSPHATE
TOGETHER TO ACD WOULD RESPECTIVELY BE?
questions.explanation:
THE STORAGE PERIOD WHEN ADDING PHOSPHATE ALONE TO ACD WOULD BE 21 DAYS AND WHEN ADDING
ADENINE AND PHOSPHATE TOGETHER WOULD BE 35 DAYS.
WHEN ADDING PHOSPHATE TO ACD, CITRATE PHOSPHATE DEXTROSE (CPD) IS FORMED – IT HAS A STORAGE
PERIOD OF 21 DAYS. THERE IS NO CHANGE IN THE SHELF LIFE AS PHOSPHATE ONLY INCREASES THE 2,3 DPG
LEVELS OF THE STORED BLOOD.
510
WHEN ADDING BOTH PHOSPHATE AND ADENINE TO ACD, CITRATE PHOSPHATE DEXTROSE ADENINE (CPDA-1)
IS FORMED. IT HAS A STORAGE PERIOD OF 35 DAYS. IT INCREASES THE SHELF LIFE BY IMPROVING ATP SYNTHESIS
OF RBCS.
USING ADDITIVE SOLUTIONS CONTAINING SALINE, ADENINE, AND GLUCOSE, WITH OR WITHOUT MANNITOL
(SAGM) DECREASES RBC HEMOLYSIS, THUS INCREASING THE STORAGE PERIOD TO 42 DAYS.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.prompt: FUNCTIONAL RESIDUAL CAPACITY IS:
options: VOLUME THAT REMAINS AFTER FORCED EXPIRATION
questions.explanation:
FUNCTIONAL RESIDUAL CAPACITY (FRC) IS EXPIRATORY RESERVE VOLUME + RESIDUAL VOLUME.
FROM THE PICTURE GIVEN BELOW, (FRC = ERV + RV).
LUNG CAPACITIES:
THE TOTAL LUNG CAPACITY CAN BE BROKEN DOWN INTO ALTERNATIVE CAPACITIES THAT HELP TO DEFINE
FUNCTIONING LUNGS.
- THE VITAL LUNG CAPACITY REFERS TO THE MAXIMUM AMOUNT OF AIR EXPIRED FROM THE FULLY INFLATED LUNG
OR MAXIMUM INSPIRATORY LEVEL.
- THE INSPIRATORY CAPACITY IS THE MAXIMUM AMOUNT OF AIR INSPIRED FROM THE END-EXPIRATORY LEVEL.
- THE FUNCTIONAL RESIDUAL CAPACITY REPRESENTS THE VOLUME OF THE AIR REMAINING IN THE LUNGS AFTER
EXPIRATION OF A NORMAL BREATH.

questions.explanation:
GUM IS THE BEST ANSWER AMONG THE GIVEN OPTIONS. EVEN THOUGH ALL OF THE GIVEN OPTIONS ARE DIETARY
FIBERS, THE CONSUMPTION OF GUMS THROUGH DIET IS VERY LOW AND HENCE, IT IS THE BEST ANSWER.
511

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.prompt: LESION IN THE MEDIAL LEMNISCUS AT THE LEVEL OF PONS CAUSES WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING?
options: PAIN AND TEMPERATURE LOSS IN THE SAME SIDE
PAIN AND TEMPERATURE LOSS IN THE OPPOSITE SIDE
LOSS OF TACTILE AND PROPRIOCEPTION ON THE SAME SIDE
LOSS OF TACTILE AND PROPRIOCEPTION ON THE OPPOSITE SIDE
questions.answer: LOSS OF TACTILE AND PROPRIOCEPTION ON THE OPPOSITE SIDE
questions.explanation:
LESION IN THE MEDIAL LEMNISCUS AT THE LEVEL OF PONS CAUSES LOSS OF TACTILE AND PROPRIOCEPTION ON THE
OPPOSITE SIDE.
FIBERS OF MEDIAL LEMNISCUS ASCEND IPSILATERALLY IN THE DORSAL COLUMNS OF THE SPINAL CORD TO THE
MEDULLA, WHERE THEY SYNAPSE IN THE GRACILUS AND CUNEATE NUCLEI.
THE SECOND-ORDER NEURONS FROM THESE NUCLEI CROSS THE MIDLINE AND ASCEND IN THE MEDIAL LEMNISCUS
TO END IN THE CONTRALATERAL VENTRAL POSTERIOR LATERAL (VPL) NUCLEUS AND RELATED SPECIFIC SENSORY
RELAY NUCLEI OF THE THALAMUS.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.prompt: WHICH NEUROTRANSMITTER IS RESPONSIBLE FOR ANTEROGRADE DILATATION OF THE SMALL INTESTINE?
questions.explanation:
VIP IS RESPONSIBLE FOR ANTEROGRADE DILATATION OF THE SMALL INTESTINE.
PERISTALSIS INVOLVES THE CONTRACTION OF A SEGMENT OF INTESTINE BEHIND THE BOLUS OF FOOD AND
RELAXATION OF A SEGMENT OF THE INTESTINE IN FRONT OF THE BOLUS OF FOOD.
CHOLINERGIC NEURONS PASSING IN ANTEROGRADE DIRECTION PRODUCE NO AND VIP WHICH CAUSE RELAXATION
OF A SEGMENT OF THE INTESTINE IN FRONT OF THE BOLUS.
CHOLINERGIC NEURONS PASSING IN RETROGRADE DIRECTION PRODUCE SUBSTANCE P AND ACETYLCHOLINE WHICH
CAUSE CONTRACTION OF A SEGMENT OF THE INTESTINE BEHIND THE BOLUS.
512
NOTE: IN ACHALASIA CARDIA, THERE IS DECREASED RELEASE OF NO AND VIP IN THE DISTAL PART OF THE
ESOPHAGUS.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.prompt: REFLEX RESPONSIBLE FOR TACHYCARDIA DURING RIGHT ATRIAL DISTENSION IS:
questions.explanation:
REFLEX RESPONSIBLE FOR TACHYCARDIA DURING RIGHT ATRIAL DISTENSION IS BAINBRIDGE REFLEX.
ATRIAL REFLEX CONTROL OF HEART RATE: THE BAINBRIDGE REFLEX
- THE STRETCH RECEPTORS OF THE ATRIA THAT ELICIT THE BAINBRIDGE REFLEX TRANSMIT THEIR AFFERENT SIGNALS
THROUGH THE VAGUS NERVES TO THE MEDULLA OF THE BRAIN.
- THEN EFFERENT SIGNALS ARE TRANSMITTED BACK THROUGH VAGAL AND SYMPATHETIC NERVES TO INCREASE
HEART RATE AND STRENGTH OF HEART CONTRACTION.
BEZOLD-JARISCH REFLEX:
- ACTIVATION OF CHEMOSENSITIVE VAGAL C FIBRES IN THE CARDIOPULMONARY REGION (E.G. JUXTA CAPILLARY
REGION OF ALVEOLI, VENTRICLES, ATRIA, GREAT VEINS, AND PULMONARY ARTERY) CAUSES PROFOUND BRADY-
CARDIA, HYPOTENSION AND A BRIEF PERIOD OF APNEA FOLLOWED BY RAPID SHALLOW BREATHING.
CUSHING REFLEX:
- WHEN ICP IS INCREASED, THE BLOOD SUPPLY TO RVLM NEURONS IS COMPROMISED.
- THE LOCAL HYPOXIA AND HYPERCAPNIA CAUSES AN INCREASE IN DISCHARGE FROM THE NEURONS, PRODUCING
HYPERTENSION, BRADYCARDIA AND IRREGULAR RESPIRATION.
- THE RESULTANT RISE IN SYSTEMIC ARTERIAL PRESSURE TENDS TO RESTORE THE BLOOD FLOW TO THE MEDULLA.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.prompt: TESTOSTERONE PRODUCTION IS MAINLY CONTRIBUTED BY ______
questions.explanation:
TESTOSTERONE PRODUCTION IS MAINLY CONTRIBUTED BY LEYDIG CELLS.
TESTOSTERONE IS SYNTHESIZED FROM CHOLESTEROL IN THE LEYDIG CELLS AND ALSO FROM ANDROSTENEDIONE

THE DIAGNOSIS OF TESTOSTERONE DEFICIENCY SHOULD BE MADE ONLY ON THE BASIS OF CLINICAL SIGNS AND
SYMPTOMS CONSISTENT WITH ANDROGEN DEFICIENCY, AND CONSISTENTLY SUBNORMAL SERUM TESTOSTERONE
CONCENTRATIONS AT 8 TO 10 AM ON THREE OCCASIONS.
TESTOSTERONE HAS BEEN USED TO TREAT PRIMARY OR SECONDARY HYPOGONADISM IN ADULT MEN.

questions.explanation:

Question No. Correct Option

questions.explanation:
HEMISECTION OF THE SPINAL CORD CAUSES DAMAGE TO ASCENDING SENSORY (DORSAL COLUMN PATHWAY,
VENTROLATERAL SPINOTHALAMIC TRACT) AND DESCENDING MOTOR (CORTICOSPINAL TRACT) PATHWAYS, WHICH IS
CALLED THE BROWN- SéQUARD SYNDROME.
THE LESION TO FASCICULUS GRACILUS OR FASCICULUS CUNEATUS LEADS TO IPSILATERAL LOSS OF DISCRIMINATIVE
TOUCH, VIBRATION, AND PROPRIOCEPTION BELOW THE LEVEL OF THE LESION.(FIBERS FROM THE SACRAL CORD ARE

THE LOSS OF THE SPINOTHALAMIC TRACT LEADS TO CONTRALATERAL LOSS OF PAIN AND TEMPERATURE SENSATION
BEGINNING ONE OR TWO SEGMENTS BELOW THE LESION.
DAMAGE TO THE CORTICOSPINAL TRACT PRODUCES WEAKNESS AND SPASTICITY IN CERTAIN MUSCLE GROUPS ON

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.prompt:
A PERSON DEVELOPS HEADACHE AND BREATHLESSNESS ON A TREKKING EXPEDITION FOLLOWING RAPID
ASCENT TO OVER 3000 METRES ABOVE THE SEA LEVEL. WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS NOT USED IN THE
TREATMENT OF THIS CONDITION?
questions.explanation:
THE SYMPTOMS OF HEADACHE AND BREATHLESSNESS FOLLOWING RAPID ASCENT INDICATE ACUTE
MOUNTAIN/ALTITUDE SICKNESS AND IV DIGOXIN IS NOT USED TO TREAT THIS CONDITION.
ON ASCENT TO HIGH ALTITUDES, THE LOW PARTIAL PRESSURE OF OXYGEN LEADS TO HYPOXIA AND SYSTEMIC
ARTERIOLAR DILATATION. CONSEQUENTLY, THE CAPILLARY PRESSURE RISES WITH INCREASED TRANSUDATION OF
FLUID INTO THE BRAIN TISSUE AND THE FOLLOWING SYMPTOMS ARE SEEN:
- HEADACHE
- IRRITATION
- INSOMNIA
- BREATHLESSNESS
- NAUSEA AND VOMITING
TREATMENT INVOLVES ADMINISTRATION OF OXYGEN, DESCENT TO A LOWER ALTITUDE AND ADMINISTRATION OF
ACETAZOLAMIDE. ACETAZOLAMIDE COUNTERACTS HYPOXIA BY STIMULATING RESPIRATION AND ALSO REDUCES THE
FORMATION OF CEREBROSPINAL FLUID, THEREBY REDUCING INTRACRANIAL TENSION.
PORTABLE HYPERBARIC CHAMBERS ARE INCREASINGLY BEING USED IN THE TREATMENT OF HIGH-ALTITUDE
ILLNESSES WHEN RAPID DESCENT IS NOT POSSIBLE. THESE CHAMBERS ARE AVAILABLE IN ARMED FORCES
HOSPITALS IN HIGH ALTITUDE AREAS

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.prompt: V/Q = INFINITY HOLDS TRUE IN WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS?
options: FOREIGN BODY OBSTRUCTION IN THE BRONCHUS
WHEN O2 AND CO2 RATIO IS EQUAL
THE PO2 OF ALVEOLAR AIR IS 159 MMHG AND PCO2 IS 40 MMHG
questions.explanation:
VA /Q= INFINITY MEANS THAT THERE IS NO EXCHANGE OF O2 & CO2, WHICH MEANS THE VOLUME OF
THE LUNG EQUALS TO DEAD SPACE AND THE PHYSIOLOGICAL EFFORT OF BREATHING IS WASTED.
VA REPRESENTS THE VENTILATION IN ALVEOLI AND Q REPRESENTS THE BLOOD FLOW THROUGH THE ALVEOLUS. THE
RATIO OF VA AND Q EXPLAINS THE RESPIRATORY EXCHANGE WHEN THERE IS AN IMBALANCE BETWEEN ALVEOLAR
VENTILATION AND ALVEOLAR BLOOD FLOW. THE VENTILATION-PERFUSION RATIO IS CONSIDERED NORMAL IF THERE IS
AN EQUAL AMOUNT OF BLOOD FLOW & VENTILATION THROUGH THE ALVEOLUS.
VA /Q RATIO IS INFINITY WHEN:
- THERE IS ADEQUATE VENTILATION BUT NO PERFUSION.
- NO EXCHANGE OF GASES ( O2 AND CO2 )THROUGH THE RESPIRATORY MEMBRANES OF CORRESPONDING
ALVEOLI.
- THE ALVEOLAR AIR EQUILIBRATES THE HUMIDIFIED INSPIRED AIR.
- PARTIAL PRESSURES OF THE O2 AND CO2 ARE 149 MMHG & 0 MM HG RESPECTIVELY.
522

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.prompt: PROLACTIN LEVEL IS HIGHEST DURING :
questions.explanation:
AMONG THE GIVEN OPTIONS, THE PROLACTIN LEVEL IS HIGHEST 24 HOURS AFTER DELIVERY.
THE MAXIMUM LEVEL OF PROLACTIN IS SEEN DURING PREGNANCY AND IN THE IMMEDIATE POSTPARTUM
PERIOD. DURING PREGNANCY, THE SECRETION IS INCREASED REACHING A PEAK AT THE TIME OF DELIVERY. AFTER
DELIVERY, THE PLASMA CONCENTRATION FALLS TO NONPREGNANT LEVELS IN A FEW WEEKS. SUCKLING PRODUCES
SURGES OF PROLACTIN RELEASE.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.prompt: C WAVE OF JVP REPRESENTS:
options: TRICUSPID BULGE INTO RIGHT ATRIUM DURING ISOVOLUMETRIC VENTRICULAR CONTRACTION
questions.answer: TRICUSPID BULGE INTO RIGHT ATRIUM DURING ISOVOLUMETRIC VENTRICULAR CONTRACTION
questions.explanation:
'C' WAVE IN JVP REPRESENTS TRICUSPID BULGE INTO RIGHT ATRIUM DURING ISOVOLUMETRIC VENTRICULAR
CONTRACTION.
CHARACTERISTICS OF JVP :
- A WAVE CORRESPONDS TO ATRIAL SYSTOLE WHICH CAUSES REGURGITATION OF SOME BLOOD INTO THE GREAT
VEINS.
- C WAVE OCCURS DUE TO THE INCREASE IN ATRIAL PRESSURE CAUSED BY BULGING OF THE TRICUSPID VALVE INTO
THE RIGHT ATRIUM DURING ISOVOLUMETRIC VENTRICULAR CONTRACTION.
- X DESCENT OCCURS DUE TO THE FALL IN ATRIAL PRESSURE DURING VENTRICULAR SYSTOLE DUE TO PULLING OF
VALVE LEAFLETS.
- V WAVE IS SEEN AT THE END OF VENTRICULAR CONTRACTION AND OCCURS DUE TO THE SLOW VENOUS FILLING
WHICH CAUSES AN INCREASE IN ATRIAL PRESSURE.
- Y DESCENT OCCURS DUE TO THE PASSIVE EMPTYING OF THE RIGHT ATRIUM INTO THE RIGHT VENTRICLE.
523

questions.prompt:
THE PROTEIN IN THE GLOMERULAR BASEMENT MEMBRANE RESPONSIBLE FOR CHARGE-DEPENDENT
FILTRATION IS?
questions.explanation:
THE PROTEIN IN THE GLOMERULAR BASEMENT MEMBRANE RESPONSIBLE FOR CHARGE-DEPENDENT FILTRATION IS
HEPARAN SULFATE. IT PREVENTS FILTRATION BY REPELLING NEGATIVELY CHARGED PROTEINS.
COLLAGEN TYPE IV, FIBRONECTIN, ENTACTIN ARE STRUCTURAL COMPONENTS OF BASEMENT MEMBRANE.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.prompt:
WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING CLOTTING FACTORS WOULD HAVE DECREASED GAMMA CARBOXYGLUTAMATE
RESIDUE IN A PATIENT ON WARFARIN THERAPY?
questions.explanation:
FACTOR 2 WOULD HAVE DECREASED GAMMA CARBOXYGLUTAMATE RESIDUE IN A PATIENT ON WARFARIN THERAPY.
ACTIVATION OF COAGULATION FACTORS II, VII, IX, X IS DONE BY CARBOXYLATION OF THEIR GLUTAMATE
RESIDUES. THIS IS DONE BY THE ENZYME γ-GLUTAMYL CARBOXYLASE WITH THE REDUCED FORM OF VITAMIN K
AS A CO-FACTOR.
THIS REDUCED FORM OF VITAMIN K NEEDS TO BE CONSTANTLY RECYCLED BACK FROM ITS OXIDIZED FORM FOR THE
REACTION TO CONTINUE. THIS RECYCLING IS DONE BY THE ENZYME VITAMIN K EPOXIDE REDUCTASE. THIS
ENZYME IS INHIBITED BY WARFARIN.
HENCE, WARFARIN INDIRECTLY INHIBITS THE γ-CARBOXYLATION OF VITAMIN K DEPENDENT CLOTTING FACTORS
- FACTORS II, VII, IX, X BY DIRECTLY INHIBITING VITAMIN K EPOXIDE REDUCTASE. THUS LEADING TO
DECREASED GAMMA CARBOXYGLUTAMATE RESIDUE IN THESE FACTORS.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS WOULD HAVE THE HIGHEST LEVELS OF ACTH AND CORTISOL?
questions.explanation:

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.prompt: FOLLOWING COMPLETE ILEAL AND PARTIAL JEJUNAL RESECTION, THE PATIENT IS MOST LIKELY TO HAVE
questions.explanation:

VITAMIN B12 IS ABSORBED IN THE ILEUM. VITAMIN B12 BINDS TO INTRINSIC FACTOR, A PROTEIN SECRETED BY
